🚨 HERE'S THE PROBLEM
- 🏛️ The government needs financing
- 🏢 Businesses need financing
- 🤖 AI companies need financing
- 🏠 Homebuyers need financing
- 🏦 And all of them are operating in a world where interest rates remain high

⚖️ They aren't borrowing from one identical pool of money, and government borrowing doesn't mechanically determine every other interest rate

💵 But high Treasury yields raise the return investors can earn from relatively safe dollar assets

🔄 That changes the alternatives available to them.

💭 Imagine a company promising enormous profits five years from now
📈 An investor must decide whether those profits justify the uncertainty when government bonds already offer substantial income

💳 And if the company itself needs billions in loans, higher interest payments make its future profits harder to achieve

🚨 THAT'S WHY THE COST OF CAPITAL MATTERS SO MUCH RIGHT NOW
📈 Not because higher interest rates automatically destroy every stock rally
🎯 But because they raise the standard that expensive investments must meet

🤖 And this brings us directly to today's biggest technology story

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3) 🤖 NVIDIA - JENSEN HUANG IS OUT
🙉HOW MUCH OF A $4 TRILLION COMPANY WAS ACTUALLY HIM?

🚨 IT'S OFFICIAL

🚨 Jensen Huang has officially stepped down as Nvidia's CEO
🏦 Colette Kress, who previously managed the company's finances, has temporarily taken his place

And look at how this happened
👀 First, reports emerged about a relationship involving a businesswoman suspected of Chinese intelligence connections

👀 Then another relationship was reported
⚠️ And then another
⏳ All within days

🤔 INTERESTING TIMING, ISN'T IT?
📊 Just as investors were already questioning whether AI companies could justify their enormous valuations
💸 Building AI infrastructure costs billions
🏦 Borrowing money remains expensive
📉 And investors are becoming less willing to pay any price for promises of future profits

💥 Then suddenly, the man who spent 33 years building Nvidia is gone

🚨 BUT THE MARKET REACTION RAISES A MUCH BIGGER QUESTION

💰 HOW MUCH OF NVIDIA'S VALUE WAS ITS TECHNOLOGY?
👤 AND HOW MUCH WAS INVESTORS' TRUST IN JENSEN HUANG?

🤔 Think about it
💾 Nvidia makes powerful computer chips that companies use to build artificial intelligence

⚙️ Those chips are still there
🏭 Its factories and manufacturing partners haven't disappeared
👨‍💻 Its engineers haven't forgotten how to design chips
📦 Its customers still need computing power

🚨 SO WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED?
💾 Not the technology overnight

🎯 THE CONFIDENCE IN WHO WILL LEAD IT TOMORROW
📉 And investors have already wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from Nvidia's market value during the selloff

🔍 Now here's where things get even more interesting
💾 Nvidia doesn't just sell chips
💰 It also invests in companies that buy those chips and helps finance parts of the AI industry

🌐 That means its influence goes far beyond its own products

🏦 If new management becomes more cautious about investing money, some businesses depending on Nvidia's support could face a much harder time financing their expansion

💸 And remember - many AI companies are already spending enormous amounts of money before they become consistently profitable

🚨 NOW ZOOM OUT
📉 If losing one CEO can shake confidence in a company worth trillions...

🤔 What does that tell us about the valuations of other AI companies built around famous founders and their promises?

💰 How much are investors paying for technology that already earns money?

👤 And how much for the belief that one particular person will deliver an extraordinary future?

🎯 NVIDIA DIDN'T LOSE ITS CHIPS
🚨 IT LOST THE MAN INVESTORS TRUSTED TO TURN THOSE CHIPS INTO TRILLIONS
💰 AND NOW WALL STREET HAS TO DECIDE HOW MUCH THAT TRUST WAS WORTH

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4) 🇪🇺 EUROPEAN STOCKS JUST HIT RECORD HIGHS WHILE AMERICAN AI STOCKS STRUGGLE

🌍 Now look across the Atlantic
🇪🇺 The Stoxx Europe 600 - an index tracking 600 major European companies - reached a new record on Thursday

🇩🇪 Germany's DAX also reached a record

📉 Yet American technology stocks have been suffering from concerns about AI valuations, financing and Nvidia's leadership crisis

🚨 WHY ARE THESE MARKETS BEHAVING DIFFERENTLY?
⚖️ Because European and American stock indexes don't contain the same businesses in the same proportions

🤖 The American market has enormous exposure to a handful of highly valued technology companies

🏭 Europe has a broader mix of industrial manufacturers, banks, healthcare businesses, consumer companies and energy producers

💰 And European corporate earnings have been strong
📈 Companies in the Stoxx 600 are on track to report approximately 25% quarterly profit growth

🏆 That's their strongest performance in four years
🔍 Now consider the difference between an AI infrastructure developer and an established European industrial business

🏗️ The AI developer may need to borrow billions to build facilities before collecting enough revenue to recover the investment

🏭 An established industrial company may already have customers, existing factories and profits

📈 Both can grow
⚠️ But the financial risks are different

💸 And some investors appear to be reducing exposure to expensive AI-linked assets while increasing exposure to other companies

🚨 THIS ISN'T THE SAME AS ALL INVESTORS ABANDONING TECHNOLOGY
💰 It's a change in what they are willing to pay for different kinds of earnings

🔍 There's another factor
🛢️ Europe imports substantial amounts of energy

⚡ If oil prices fall and those savings eventually reach businesses, some European manufacturers and consumers could benefit

🏦 But persistent inflation and higher interest rates remain risks for Europe too

🚨 SO THE IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENT IS NOT THAT EUROPE HAS MAGICALLY ESCAPED GLOBAL PROBLEMS

🎯 It's that investors are finding opportunities outside the most crowded AI investments
💰 And those opportunities are supported by actual corporate earnings

🎯 A WEAK AI TRADE DOESN'T AUTOMATICALLY MEAN A WEAK GLOBAL STOCK MARKET
💰 CAPITAL CAN LEAVE ONE GROUP OF COMPANIES AND FIND A NEW HOME IN ANOTHER

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5) 🇺🇦 UKRAINE - EUROPE IS MOVING CLOSER TO THE NEGOTIATING TABLE
🕊️PEACE IS STILL NOT AGREED

🕊️ The diplomatic process has advanced
🇺🇸 US representatives have completed meetings with Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin

🤝 A new negotiating round is being prepared

🇪🇺 And Washington says European representatives should participate directly

🔄 That would be a significant change from the earlier three-party format involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States

⚠️ But there is still no ceasefire
🗺️ The territorial dispute remains unresolved
🇷🇺 And Russia continues rejecting the possibility of foreign military forces being stationed in Ukraine

🚨 SO WHAT HAS ACTUALLY IMPROVED?
🤝 The negotiating format may become broader
🕊️ The parties are continuing discussions
🔓 And a major prisoner exchange has been agreed in principle

✅ Those developments matter
⚠️ But they don't settle the conditions required to end the fighting

🚨 NOW LOOK AT ANOTHER DEVELOPMENT THAT DESERVES ATTENTION
🇺🇦 Ukraine says it is experiencing restrictions affecting Starshield
🛰️ Starshield is the military satellite communications service built by SpaceX, Elon Musk's space company
📡 Ukraine uses it for military communications and drone operations
🚁 Ukrainian officials say the service has been restricted in ways that affect fast-moving drones
⚖️ SpaceX disputes the claim that it changed the service
🔍 The cause of the reported disruption has not been established independently

🚨 BUT THE STRATEGIC RISK IS CLEAR
📡 Modern military operations depend heavily on communications infrastructure
🏢 And that infrastructure can be controlled by commercial companies and foreign governments
🛡️ So security guarantees aren't only about soldiers, tanks and missiles
🛰️ They also involve access to satellites, communications networks, maintenance and technology
💰 And those systems require contracts, suppliers and long-term funding

🚨 THIS IS THE BIGGER QUESTION BEHIND A FUTURE PEACE AGREEMENT
🛡️ Who guarantees Ukraine's security?
💰 Who pays for it?
🛰️ Who controls the technology it relies on?
⚠️ And what happens if access to that technology changes?

🌍 A meeting in Abu Dhabi, Moscow or Dublin cannot answer those questions by itself
🎯 THE NEGOTIATING PROCESS IS MOVING
🔐 THE SECURITY SYSTEM THAT WOULD MAKE PEACE LAST STILL HAS TO BE AGREED AND FINANCED

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6) 🟠 BITCOIN BELOW $69K 
🙉 REMEMBER WHAT WE'VE BEEN WARNING ABOUT SINCE AUGUST?

🍊 FIRST THEY SOLD YOU UPT0BER
🌕 THEN MOONVEMBER
📅 THEN THE MAGICAL FOURTH QUARTER
🇺🇸 THEN THE POST-ELECTION RALLY
📊 THEN ANOTHER HISTORICAL STATISTIC

🚨 AND WHEN THAT DIDN'T WORK?
🎭 They found another reason Bitcoin was supposedly about to explode

🚨 WE KEPT TALKING ABOUT SOMETHING ELSE
💰 THE ACTUAL MONEY AVAILABLE TO BUY BITCOIN

⚠️ Since August, we've repeatedly warned that the conditions for a sustained rally were weak
📉 Not because of some magical chart pattern
🔮 Not because of a feeling

🌍 But because the bigger financial picture wasn't supporting the promises
🛢️ Energy disruptions were feeding inflation
🏦 Borrowing money remained expensive
💵 Investors could earn attractive returns without taking enormous risks
🤖 Billions were flowing into AI infrastructure
📉 And crypto was struggling to attract enough sustained buying

🚨 WE KEPT ASKING THE SAME QUESTION
🤔 WHERE IS THE MONEY SUPPOSED TO COME FROM TO SUPPORT ALL THESE BULLISH TARGETS?

📅 Because a calendar doesn't buy Bitcoin
📊 A historical average doesn't buy Bitcoin
💸 And calling November bullish doesn't magically create another billion dollars of demand

🚨 NOW LOOK WHERE WE ARE:
- 🟠 Bitcoin has fallen below $69,000
- 📉 It traded around $67,400 during the selloff
- 💥 Approximately $1.47 BILLION in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated within 24 hours
- 📉 Of that, around $1.31 BILLION came from traders betting on rising prices

🚨 NOW HERE'S ANOTHER NUMBER PEOPLE ARE CELEBRATING
📊 Bitcoin dominance has climbed above 61%
📈 Some are calling that bullish

🛑 BUT HOLD ON
🟠 Bitcoin dominance simply tells us how much of the total crypto market's value belongs to Bitcoin

📉 Imagine Bitcoin falls 5%
💥 But smaller cryptocurrencies fall 15%
📊 Bitcoin's share of the market rises

🚨 EVEN THOUGH BITCOIN ITSELF IS LOSING VALUE
🏦 No magical institutional buying required
❌ No new bull market confirmed
📉 Just other crypto assets falling even harder

🚨 AND LOOK AT THE ACTUAL MONEY FLOWS
💸 US investment funds holding Bitcoin directly have been experiencing withdrawals
📉 Some companies have reduced their Bitcoin holdings
🏦 Strategy, one of the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holders, is being removed from major stock indexes

📊 That last development may force certain investment funds to sell Strategy shares because they must follow those indexes
⚖️ It doesn't automatically mean Strategy must sell its Bitcoin
💳 But it could make future fundraising more difficult or expensive

🚨 SEE WHAT WE'VE BEEN TRYING TO EXPLAIN?
🟠 The problem was never that Bitcoin couldn't bounce
📈 Of course it could
🔄 And it still can

⚠️ The problem was that a sustainable bull market needs more than temporary rebounds, borrowed money and seasonal promises
💰 It needs investors willing to commit real capital and keep buying when others sell
🌍 And the wider financial environment matters enormously

🚨 WE DIDN'T NEED TO PREDICT THE EXACT DAY BITCOIN WOULD FALL
🔍 We needed to recognize that the conditions being advertised as bullish were much weaker than the headlines suggested

📅 That's what we've been discussing for months
📉 And now the selling, fund withdrawals and forced liquidations are giving us more evidence of that pressure

🚨 SO BEFORE SOMEONE SELLS YOU THE NEXT MAGICAL DATE...
🎯 Ask them one simple question
💰 WHERE ARE THE BUYERS?

❌ Not the predictions
📊 Not the historical charts
🎭 Not the motivational speeches

💰 THE ACTUAL MONEY!
📅 Because the market doesn't care whether it's October, November, Thursday or Veterans Day

🚨 THE MARKET NEEDS BUYERS
📉 AND IF THEY AREN'T STRONG ENOUGH TO ABSORB THE SELLERS, THE PRICE FALLS

🎯 THEY FOLLOWED THE CALENDAR
💰 WE FOLLOWED THE CAPITAL

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7) ✴️ CRYPTO- HACKERS STOLE MORE THAN THE INDUSTRY'S ESTIMATED ON-CHAIN REVENUE
⚠️BUT READ THE NUMBERS CAREFULLY

🚨 THIS MAY BE THE MOST IMPORTANT CRYPTO BUSINESS STORY OF THE DAY

📊 According to DefiLlama, approximately:
💸 $8.78 BILLION has been lost to cryptocurrency hacks in 2026

🔍 Meanwhile, research from ARK Invest estimates approximately:
💰 $5.6 BILLION in annual on-chain revenue for the industry

⚠️ The losses from hacks already exceed that revenue estimate

🚨 BUT DON'T MISUNDERSTAND THE COMPARISON
⚖️ These figures measure different things
🔓 The losses represent assets stolen from users, platforms and protocols

⛓️ The revenue estimate measures money earned through activity on blockchain-based services
📊 They aren't two sides of one company's income statement

💰 And they don't mean the entire cryptocurrency industry has made a net loss equal to the difference

🔍 There's another detail
💥 The enormous Binance hack accounts for approximately $6.36 billion of the reported losses
📉 That single incident represents more than 70% of the annual total

⚠️ So one extraordinary attack heavily influences the headline
🛡️ But even after making that distinction, the security problem is serious

🚨 BECAUSE THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM DOESN'T GROW ON TRANSACTION SPEED ALONE

🤝 It also needs trust
🏦 A bank must protect customer assets
💳 A payment company must prevent fraud
🔐 An exchange must secure its systems
🛡️ And investors need confidence that the infrastructure holding their money won't fail

🔍 Now compare this with what traditional finance is doing
🇩🇪 Deutsche Börse, one of Europe's major exchange groups, has expanded blockchain-based trading in tokenized versions of Germany's 40 largest listed companies

⛓️ Those tokens are backed by real shares held with a regulated custodian and can trade around the clock through participating venues

🌍 This creates new distribution opportunities
⚖️ But tokenized shares remain subject to legal, custody and market-structure requirements
📜 They aren't automatically identical in every respect to holding ordinary shares directly
🔐 And as more financial activity moves onto digital networks, security becomes even more important

🚨 THAT'S WHERE THE NEXT BIG BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY MAY EMERGE
🪙 Not simply issuing another token
🏦 But providing reliable custody
🔍 Transaction monitoring
🛡️ Cybersecurity
⚖️ Regulated settlement

💰 And financial services customers are prepared to pay for

🎯 CRYPTO ADOPTION IS CREATING REAL BUSINESSES
🚨 CRYPTO SECURITY FAILURES ARE ALSO CREATING ENORMOUS REAL COSTS

⚖️ Both are part of the same industry's future

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🏁 NOVEMBER 13 - WHERE ARE WE RIGHT NOW?

🛢️ ENERGY
🌍 The world is producing more oil, but damaged infrastructure and expensive fuel haven't magically recovered

🏦 INTEREST RATES
🔥 Inflation remains a problem
💳 Borrowing is still expensive
🇺🇸 And the US government itself is paying enormous amounts just to service its debt

🤖 ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
💾 AI technology is still advancing
🏗️ But companies need extraordinary amounts of money to build the infrastructure behind it
📉 And Nvidia just showed how quickly investors can lose confidence when the leadership behind those promises changes

🇪🇺 STOCK MARKETS
📈 European stocks have been reaching records while American technology shares face pressure
💰 Money hasn't stopped moving
🔄 Investors are simply making different choices about where to put it

🇺🇦 GEOPOLITICS
🤝 More meetings
🕊️ More promises of progress
⚠️ Still no peace agreement
🌍 And until the actual conflicts are resolved, the economic costs and security risks remain

🟠 BITCOIN
📉 Below $69,000
💥 Billions in selling pressure and forced liquidations
📅 And once again, the calendar failed to deliver the bull market everyone promised

✴️ CRYPTO
🏦 Banks are building new blockchain services
💸 But hackers have stolen billions, and investors are still pulling money from parts of the market

🚨 ADOPTION IS GROWING
🚫THAT DOESN'T MEAN EVERY CRYPTO INVESTMENT IS WINNING

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔮 SO WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE THE MARKET?

🎯 Let's make this simple
🌍 First, we need real progress in reducing global conflicts

🛢️ That could help restore reliable energy supplies and bring costs down

🔥 Lower costs could help inflation cool

🏦 Lower inflation could give central banks room to stop raising interest rates - and eventually make borrowing cheaper

📈 And that could help stocks, Bitcoin and other risky investments attract more money

🚨 BUT HERE'S THE IMPORTANT PART
📊 Markets don't have to wait for every step to happen before they rise

⚠️ And that's exactly where the danger lies

🚨 THEN THE PROMISES GET MORE EXPENSIVE TO BELIEVE

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Anchor: Let's get back to our top story. The scandal that came out of the tech giant Nvidia and led to the ousting of their CEO founder, President Jensen Huang in less than a week. As of today, Huang's resignation is effective immediately, but let's take a look at how we got here. In a message to his staff on Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Who is suffering but will be in good shape by the end? Reporter: I had a follow up in video question. I was curious if the FBI ever considered giving Jensen Huang a defensive counterintelligence briefing. And if so, if not, why not?

Todd Blanche: Well, there's no scenario which I could talk about why we would or would not give somebody a defensive intelligence briefing, but there's a lot of and why it would be the FBI by the way as opposed to another agency. It depends on the circumstances. And normally defensive briefings. And I say normally 'cause there's exceptions, but normally defensive briefings are to protect somebody's life, right? So if there's a threat that intelligence hears about or the FBI hears about, then of course we will do a defensive briefing. I'm not sure that that's what this was.

Reporter: When did the Justice Department learn with regard to Nvidia that Alice Huang might be a suspected Chinese asset? And there's been concerns raised that the Commerce Department was giving favoritism to Nvidia and Megaspeed, which is Alice Huang's company. Do you share the concerns that maybe the Commerce Department was impeding the ability to uncover the smuggling network that Alice Huang was involved in?

Todd Blanche: Well, your first question assumes something that I have never said and that I don't know how to be true, so you assume that DOJ learns that she is in fact a spy. Nobody said that, I certainly haven't said that. And I don't, all I said a minute ago and all that I think I will say is that of course DOJ is investigating or looking at it. So there's no conclusions reached by the Department of Justice or by me or by Director Patel around who she is or is not. I don't have concerns with the Commerce Department. I don't, we have a good relationship with the Commerce Department. I've read some of the stories which are sourced or not sourced and so I don't have any, but no, I don't have, the answer to your question is no, I don't have any concerns.

Anchor: Meanwhile, flowers were seen laid outside the company's headquarters today as employees learned about Jensen Huang's resignation. Now amid the scandal, the company is on track to lose more than 700 billion dollars since the close of trading last week. CBS News Bay Area reporter Drew Andre is at NVIDIA headquarters in Santa Clara and has details on the next steps for this multi-trillion dollar company.

Drew Andre: The 12,000 plus employees that work here at NVIDIA's headquarters in Santa Clara woke up to this news this morning. At least for now, the company's CFO will be the one taking over as top boss. Employees pulled into NVIDIA headquarters Thursday morning, business as usual, but this week's felt far from it. NVIDIA makes a key product for AI. That product's still gonna be bought and can the new leader lead them forward on that basis? NVIDIA's chief financial officer for more than a decade steps in as interim CEO while the board decides the future. Colette Kress is a tech finance veteran before NVIDIA serving as CFO at Cisco and previously a division CFO at Microsoft. This morning, she said in a statement, NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers, and shareholders.

Steve Solomon: There will be lawsuits.

Drew Andre: UC Berkeley law professor Steve Solomon says this will be litigated because of the hundreds of billions of dollars of value that have been lost.

Steve Solomon: What those lawsuits will turn out to be, we don't know. We don't know what the board knew or could have known about what Jensen Huang was doing.

Drew Andre: US intelligence agencies believe the woman linked to Huang was a Chinese spy. The company's board is investigating the allegations Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, all leaving more questions about the company's future and market value.

Man: NVIDIA is AI and AI is NVIDIA. And also NVIDIA is retirement accounts for 401(k) accounts. So about 50 million Americans.

Drew Andre: NVIDIA was founded back in 1993 in San Jose. They went public in the late nineties and Jensen Huang has been the CEO that entire time.

Anchor: Okay, let's bring in Paul R. La Monica. He's a Barron's senior markets analysis writer. Paul, thank you for being with us. Jensen Huang resigns. So what happens now and what does NVIDIA need to do to stabilize the company?

Paul R. La Monica: Yeah, it's a great question. There are a lot of concerns about what is next. I think the first step in naming Colette Kress as the interim CEO is a way to try and right the ship, having another person who is a veteran at NVIDIA leading for the time being. And what's interesting is that prediction markets as of right now, even though you had the president talking about, you know, Tim Cook should be the CEO of NVIDIA, the predictions markets seem to think that if it's not Colette Kress that is named the permanent CEO, that it will be someone named Ian Buck, who is a GM of hyperscale and high performance computing at NVIDIA. So I think Wall Street wants stability and continuity is, you know, Jensen Huang's reason for being ousted or stepping down has nothing to do with the performance at the company per se, it's the scandal. And I think that, you know, investors want to see someone who is an NVIDIA veteran continue to lead that company.

Anchor: Yeah, let's lean into that a little bit about this post Jensen Huang era and NVIDIA. What changes within the company do you expect to see and can NVIDIA continue to thrive without Jensen? Could anybody fill his shoes?

Paul R. La Monica: His leather jacket, if you will.

Anchor: I should say the leather jacket.

Paul R. La Monica: Yes, exactly. I mean, what's gonna be fascinating is NVIDIA will report its latest earnings next week and they're gonna be phenomenal. Analysts on Wall Street expect revenue and profit to nearly double. The company still is a leader obviously in the AI chip world. The problem and what's fascinating is when you look at the stocks that rallied today in the semiconductor space, Broadcom and AMD, two top rivals of NVIDIA. So I think investors are gonna be worried that maybe now if you're a company like AMD or Broadcom, you can go to Microsoft, Amazon, the big hyperscalers like Alphabet, Google owner Alphabet as well and you can make the case. NVIDIA is in trouble. They have turmoil right now. Come to us, you can get your chips from us and that could be a potential problem for NVIDIA over the long haul if they start to lose market share and revenue to some of these rivals.

Anchor: Okay, so we're talking about NVIDIA specifically, but what about the impact on the global AI industry now that one of its most influential players, if not the most influential players is off the chessboard, at least for now?

Paul R. La Monica: Yeah, I think it's probably more symbolic than anything else. There already have been concerns about maybe the big hyperscalers would have to pull back on spending on AI in 2027, just because there have been so many worries about how much cash these companies are spending. Some companies like Oracle even using debt sales to finance their AI spending. We've seen what happened to CoreWeave, a big NVIDIA partner and company that NVIDIA is actually invested in, getting hit by worries about its spending. So I don't think that changes because of Jensen Huang being off of the table, so to speak, but it is a symbolic blow to the AI economy. He really was one of the main faces for this AI revolution.

Anchor: Paul R. La Monica, thanks so much.

Paul R. La Monica: Good to be with you.

U.S. futures were mixed as of 06:57 ART, with S&P 500 E-minis up 0.07%, Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.16% and Dow futures up 0.11%. People's Bank of China data showed new yuan loans of CNY 11.42 trillion in January–October, down from CNY 11.52 trillion through September, implying a contraction of about CNY 100 billion in October, the first monthly decline in two months; Reuters said economists had expected an increase of about CNY 800 billion. Aggregate financing totaled CNY 28.61 trillion in the first ten months. Germany's economy ministry said in its monthly report that leading indicators have stabilized but the recovery has not yet reached the labor market, and that pressures on the economy are likely to ease by year-end.

• Tech: A Reuters review identified more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around Nvidia's $NVDA restricted processors, including buildings and infrastructure, even though the company has said U.S. export controls have effectively shut it out of China's AI data-center market. In an update on Thursday's outage, Microsoft $MSFT said it was seeing early signs of stabilization, had completed recovery actions across portions of the affected infrastructure in Asia-Pacific and was extending them to other regions, with traffic being restored gradually. It extended its email timeout window to 48 hours to help protect delayed messages. The Bank of England said its critical operations were not affected.

• Geopolitics: In a confidential quarterly report to member states seen by Reuters and AP, the IAEA said it cannot conclude that Iran has not diverted nuclear material from peaceful uses, and that it does not know the exact location of the Isfahan enrichment plant Iran declared in June 2025 or whether nuclear material is present there; apart from the Bushehr power plant, it has had no access. Ukraine's energy ministry said overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure left some consumers in 12 regions without power. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia is ready to carry out a humanitarian operation to evacuate civilians from Kostiantynivka if security guarantees are given, and called on Washington to use its influence on Kyiv to agree to it. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia does not want her to represent the EU at peace talks. Euroclear Chief Executive Valérie Urbain told Le Soir there is still no miracle solution on frozen Russian assets.

text:
The Great Reset is a World Economic Forum (WEF) initiative launched in June 2020 by Klaus Schwab (and involving then-Prince Charles) as a proposed post-COVID economic recovery framework. It is not a formal binding treaty or single detailed plan, but a set of advocacy ideas promoted through Davos meetings, publications, and partnerships.⁠

Stated Goals
According to Schwab and WEF materials, the main components were:

Moving toward stakeholder capitalism (companies considering employees, communities, environment, etc., not just shareholders) via coordinated taxes, regulations, trade rules, and fiscal policies for “fairer outcomes.”
Directing pandemic recovery spending and private/pension capital toward green infrastructure, sustainability, and stronger ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) metrics to build a more “resilient, equitable, and sustainable” system.
Using technologies of the Fourth Industrial Revolution to address health, social, and public-good challenges. It was framed around UN Sustainable Development Goals and the idea that the pandemic created a “rare but narrow window of opportunity to reflect, reimagine, and reset our world.
The initiative was light on concrete, enforceable policies and more of a high-level agenda from an elite public-private organization. The WEF has described it as a commitment to build fairer, more sustainable foundations after COVID exposed existing weaknesses.

Criticisms and the “Conspiracy” Layer
Critics (especially on the political right) view it as a top-down globalist push for greater elite/government influence over economies, accelerated green transitions that can raise energy costs and reduce reliability, expanded ESG/social metrics, and reduced emphasis on traditional national sovereignty or shareholder capitalism. The famous “You’ll own nothing and be happy” meme originated from a 2016 WEF-published essay by Danish politician Ida Auken imagining a 2030 sharing-economy future (she later clarified it was not her utopia); it became a symbol of fears about property rights and control even though Schwab did not write those exact words.

Broader conspiracy claims (engineered pandemic as pretext for totalitarian control, mass property confiscation, forced digital IDs/CBDCs for total surveillance, population reduction, etc.) amplified far beyond the official initiative. Fact-checkers and mainstream outlets have repeatedly called those extreme versions false or unsupported, while noting the WEF’s influence, vague messaging, and elite membership provided fertile ground for suspicion.⁠

President Trump’s Position
Trump has long opposed the style of globalism associated with the WEF and similar agendas. In a 2019 UN speech he said the future “does not belong to globalists” but to patriots and sovereign nations.⁠Youtu

His policies emphasize America First priorities—energy abundance (fossil fuels, nuclear, reduced regulatory barriers), reindustrialization/tariffs, skepticism of aggressive climate mandates, border control, and reducing bureaucracy—which contrast with the Great Reset’s emphasis on coordinated green transitions, stakeholder/ESG frameworks, and multilateral “reset” rhetoric.

In his January 21, 2026 address at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Trump directly criticized the associated energy policies. He referred to the “Green New Scam,” called it “perhaps the greatest hoax in history,” noted that the U.S. avoided the “catastrophic energy collapse” seen in European nations that pursued similar approaches, and highlighted opening energy production, rejecting ineffective windmills that “destroy your land,” and prioritizing affordable reliable energy over green mandates. Commentators highlighted the irony of him delivering this message at the WEF, the same venue where the Great Reset was launched years earlier.⁠

He has also opposed central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), which some link to Great Reset-style control mechanisms, stating he would never allow one that gives government absolute control over money.

In short: the Great Reset is a real WEF-promoted framework for post-COVID recovery centered on stakeholder capitalism, sustainability/ESG, and tech-enabled change. Trump and his administration represent a clear policy and rhetorical counter to its globalist and green-energy pillars, prioritizing national sovereignty, energy realism, and domestic economic priorities instead

text:
Since Bank of America analyst Michael Hartnett coined the term "Magnificent Seven" in 2023, Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Tesla have consistently accounted for roughly 25% to over 30% of the S&P 500's total weight, serving as the ultimate bellwether for global capital markets.
However, as we move through the second half of 2026, these seven tech giants—which once moved in lockstep—are experiencing a profound structural divergence. 

1. Core Landscapes and Economic Moats

Despite sharp divergences in earnings and stock performance, these seven titans continue to control the most critical infrastructure and traffic gateways of the global tech ecosystem:

• NVIDIA ($NVDA): The undisputed hegemon of global AI computing infrastructure. With over 90% of its revenue stemming from its data center business, NVIDIA maintains an extraordinary moat in AI chip design and software ecosystems.

• Microsoft ($MSFT): Leveraging its enterprise software dominance and the Azure cloud platform (which recently posted 48% growth), Microsoft remains one of the most resilient players in B2B AI commercialization.

• Alphabet ($GOOGL): Retaining its global crown in digital advertising and search, Alphabet has seen explosive AI-driven momentum in Google Cloud, with single-quarter revenue surpassing $30.7 billion.

• Amazon ($AMZN): A dual powerhouse in global e-commerce and cloud computing. Its AWS division recently accelerated to 39.3% year-over-year growth, marking a near five-year high.

• Apple ($AAPL): Boasting the world’s largest premium consumer hardware ecosystem and on-device entry point, Apple has exercised rare restraint in heavy AI infrastructure spending.
• Meta Platforms ($META): Powered by a multi-billion-user social media matrix, Meta continues to leverage AI algorithms to boost ad monetization efficiency, maintaining a robust 26% top-line growth rate.

• Tesla ($TSLA): A global leader in electric vehicles and energy storage. Tesla is aggressively pivoting its strategic focus toward Full Self-Driving (FSD) and embodied AI, though its core automotive business faces near-term margin pressures.

2. Late 2026 Market Dynamics: The "AI Investment Paradox" of Rising Revenue and Falling Stocks

According to 36Kr's In-Depth Analysis of the Magnificent Seven's Q3 2026 Earnings, big tech delivered a dramatic "grow more, drop more" paradox during the autumn 2026 earnings season:
• Blockbuster Cloud Earnings Met with Sell-offs: Google Cloud’s Q3 revenue surged 103% year-over-year, yet Alphabet’s stock plunged 12.64% the following day. Amazon’s AWS hit a five-year growth high, only for its shares to tumble over 7% in after-hours trading. Meta delivered 26% revenue growth, yet its stock similarly dropped 7%.
• CapEx Devouring Free Cash Flow: Investor anxiety centers on when this astronomical cash burn will peak. As highlighted in Anue's Report on AI Investment Returns for the Magnificent Seven, massive data center build-outs have flipped Amazon’s trailing 12-month free cash flow from a $14.8 billion inflow to a $42.4 billion outflow. Meta’s free cash flow turned negative for the first time in over a decade, while Alphabet’s long-term debt ballooned from roughly $20 billion to $125 billion.
• "Asset-Light" Discipline Rewarded: Among the seven, Apple—having largely avoided blind spending on heavy AI infrastructure—has rallied roughly 26.7% year-to-date in 2026, making it the group's top performer. Meanwhile, despite declining operating profits, Tesla won over investors and stabilized its share price by announcing a reduction in full-year CapEx from $25 billion to $20 billion.

3. Underlying Risks and Future Outlook

Standing at the close of 2026, investors evaluating the future trajectory of the Magnificent Seven are closely watching three pivotal variables:
• Policy and Physical Bottlenecks in Compute Infrastructure: Surging power consumption and land use by data centers are triggering local pushback. During the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, 40 out of 41 local ballot measures across 10 states regarding data centers leaned toward restricting development. This could materially impact compute expansion plans for 2028 and beyond, directly affecting long-term order visibility for upstream chipmakers like NVIDIA.
• Spillover of Tech Credit Risk: To finance hundreds of billions of dollars in AI infrastructure, tech giants have become major borrowers in the bond market. Concerns over the sustainability of massive CapEx are now spilling over from equities into corporate credit markets.
• Reshaping of the Global Tech Landscape: Breakthroughs in cost and efficiency by open-source large language models (such as DeepSeek) are challenging the North American giants' monopoly narrative over compute and foundational models, forcing global capital to reassess tech valuations and moat durability.

text:
13 November 2026 | Daily Edition: Pre-Market
28 developments stood out across crypto overnight, spanning Bitcoin's break below $70K, leveraged liquidations, ETF withdrawals, stablecoin contraction, corporate treasury stress, Binance recovery, security, regulation, prediction markets, DeFi, tokenization and protocol development.

1⃣ Bitcoin broke below $70K and briefly traded under $68K

Bitcoin extended its decline overnight, falling through $70,000 and briefly reaching approximately $67.9K-$68.4K, its lowest level since August.

Ethereum declined toward $1,920, BNB moved into the low $-630s, Solana fell below $80 and XRP traded around $1.

Total crypto market capitalization declined toward approximately $2.35T.

🖊️ Market significance: Bitcoin has now lost several important support levels in succession, confirming that the deterioration is no longer confined to weaker altcoins.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The break below $70K changes the structure materially. I would now treat $70K as resistance rather than support, and I would not assume the decline is exhausted simply because the move has become extended.

2⃣ Market breadth deteriorated further

Bitcoin dominance remained around 59%, while Ethereum, Solana and XRP continued underperforming.

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell toward 20, firmly inside Extreme Fear.

Unlike earlier phases of weakness, Bitcoin itself is now absorbing significant selling rather than acting as the defensive destination within crypto.

🖊️ Market significance: A falling market accompanied by weak breadth and extreme sentiment indicates broad risk reduction rather than rotation between cryptoassets.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is not an altcoin washout with Bitcoin holding firm. The entire crypto risk complex is being repriced, which makes relative-strength arguments less useful until Bitcoin itself stabilizes.

3⃣ Liquidations surged toward $1.47B

Approximately $1.47B of crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours.

Around $1.31B came from leveraged longs, with nearly $800M reportedly liquidated during a four-hour period around Bitcoin's break below $70K.

More than 175,000 traders were liquidated in the referenced snapshot.

🖊️ Market significance: The liquidation cascade amplified spot selling and accelerated the move through major support levels.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is a meaningful leverage reset, but I would not call it complete simply because the liquidation number is large. What matters next is whether funding, open interest and dip-buying leverage actually normalize.

4⃣ Stablecoin supply continued contracting

Total dollar-stablecoin supply fell toward approximately $289.1B, down around 1.5% over seven days and roughly 4.9% over 30 days.

The contraction has continued alongside falling crypto prices and ETF withdrawals.

🖊️ Market significance: Stablecoin contraction indicates that part of the weakness reflects declining crypto-native dollar liquidity rather than capital simply moving from one token to another.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This remains one of the most important signals in the market. Price can rebound temporarily without new liquidity, but a sustained recovery becomes much harder when the stablecoin base is shrinking at the same time.

5⃣ Bitcoin ETFs recorded a sixth consecutive outflow session

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost approximately $47.8M on November 12.

The six-session outflow sequence from November 5 through November 12 now totals approximately $1.49B.

Bitwise's BITB and ARKB recorded meaningful withdrawals, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT attracted a small inflow.

🖊️ Market significance: Regulated institutional demand has remained negative throughout Bitcoin's decline rather than stepping in aggressively as prices fell.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Six consecutive outflow sessions matter more than any single day's number. Until that sequence breaks, I would not assume institutional investors are treating lower prices as an attractive accumulation opportunity.

6⃣ Ethereum ETFs also recorded a sixth consecutive negative session

Ethereum ETFs lost approximately $8M on November 12.

The amount was much smaller than the previous day's roughly $145M withdrawal, but the direction remained negative.

🖊️ Market significance: Ethereum's institutional flow profile remains weak even after ETH moved materially lower.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Smaller outflows are an improvement in pace, not a reversal in demand. I would need to see sustained positive sessions before interpreting lower ETH prices as attracting meaningful regulated capital.

7⃣ Solana ETFs returned to a small inflow

Solana investment products recorded approximately $1.7M of net inflows, ending their recent sequence of withdrawals.

XRP products were approximately flat, while Zcash products experienced additional outflows.

The broader U.S. spot-crypto ETF complex remained negative overall.

🖊️ Market significance: Solana showed isolated improvement even while institutional crypto flows remained broadly weak.

🗨️ My viewpoint: One positive session is worth noting but not extrapolating. I would watch whether SOL can develop a genuine flow divergence from BTC and ETH or whether this proves to be a one-day exception.

8⃣ Treasury yields remained above 5% ahead of PPI

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained around 5.12%-5.13%, while the 30-year traded around 5.45%-5.46%.

Markets continued pricing another Federal Reserve hike in December, with a smaller probability of a larger 50-basis-point move.

October PPI is due at 8:30 AM EST.

🖊️ Market significance: Elevated long-term yields increase the opportunity cost of holding risk assets and continue tightening financial conditions.

🗨️ My viewpoint: PPI is now the immediate macro trigger. A hot print would reinforce the combination already hurting crypto: restrictive policy, high real yields and weak liquidity. I would not front-run a macro reversal before seeing the data.

9⃣ Binance said all assets affected by the $6.3B hack had been replaced

Binance announced that it had fully replaced the assets affected by its recent security breach using SAFU reserves, excess futures-insurance reserves and corporate treasury resources.

The exchange published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot covering approximately 198 tokens and committed to rebuilding SAFU toward roughly $1B.

Withdrawals continued reopening in phases.

🖊️ Market significance: Full asset replacement reduces the immediate solvency concern surrounding the exchange and shifts attention toward operational recovery and transparency.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This materially improves the financial side of the Binance story, but it does not close the operational one. Restoring assets is different from proving that the authorization weakness which caused the breach has been permanently fixed.

🔟 U.S. authorities moved against more than $1.2B of stolen Binance assets

The U.S. government moved to seize or restrain more than $1.2B of assets linked to the Binance theft.

Combined public- and private-sector intervention has reportedly frozen more than $2.7B.

The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor operation.

🖊️ Market significance: Large-scale asset recovery reduces the economic benefit of major exchange thefts and demonstrates increasingly coordinated enforcement across blockchain networks and centralized issuers.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The important development is the recovery architecture. Crypto crime remains large, but tracing, freezing and cross-jurisdiction coordination are becoming much faster than they were several years ago.

1⃣1⃣ TRM Labs launched a dedicated crypto seizure service

TRM Labs introduced Beacon Concierge, allowing verified law-enforcement agencies to coordinate directly with exchanges and stablecoin issuers to freeze and seize digital assets.

Its underlying network reportedly includes more than 200 organizations covering around 80% of crypto trading volume.

The system has already helped freeze more than $35M across multiple investigations.

🖊️ Market significance: Blockchain surveillance and asset-freezing infrastructure are becoming institutionalized rather than handled through ad hoc cooperation.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This changes the economics of crypto crime. The ability to move stolen assets onchain remains, but converting those assets into usable value becomes harder when exchanges and issuers coordinate at network scale.

1⃣2⃣ Trezor identified malicious hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets

Trezor discovered malicious hardware modifications in three Safe 5 devices purchased through former Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.

The company said no customer funds were reported lost.

Firmware version 2.13.1 now blocks the implants identified so far, while Trezor has reduced its authorized reseller network substantially.

🖊️ Market significance: The incident highlights hardware supply-chain risk even when the wallet manufacturer itself has not suffered a software compromise.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Hardware wallets are only as trustworthy as the path from manufacturer to user. Supply-chain verification needs to become part of custody security, not an assumption made after the device leaves the factory.

1⃣3⃣ Osmosis stopped producing blocks

The Osmosis blockchain stalled at approximately block 74,955,152.

Upbit and Bithumb suspended OSMO deposits and withdrawals, while Coinbase reported processing disruption.

Trading remained available on affected exchanges.

🖊️ Market significance: Network halts can interrupt settlement, withdrawals and arbitrage even when exchange trading itself remains available.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is a reminder that blockchain uptime is financial infrastructure. A chain that stops producing blocks does not merely face a technical outage; it temporarily loses settlement finality.

1⃣4⃣ The White House nominated four new SEC and CFTC commissioners

Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, while Kristin Johnson and Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC.

All nominations require Senate confirmation.

Several nominees have direct experience with digital-asset policy and U.S. crypto market-structure legislation.

🖊️ Market significance: The composition of the SEC and CFTC could materially influence the regulation of crypto market structure, perpetual futures, tokenization and prediction markets.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Personnel matters when regulation is still being built. The next phase of U.S. crypto policy will increasingly depend on how these agencies interpret jurisdiction in practice rather than what Congress writes in principle.

1⃣5⃣ Louisiana sued ten prediction-market operators

Louisiana filed legal action against ten prediction-market companies, including Kalshi, Polymarket, Robinhood, Coinbase, Crypto .com, Gemini, ForecastEx, Novig, Underdog and ProphetX.

The state argues that sports-event contracts offered by these platforms constitute illegal gambling rather than federally protected derivatives activity.

Louisiana became the 11th U.S. state to pursue legal action against prediction-market operators.

🖊️ Market significance: Prediction markets increasingly face a fragmented legal environment in which federal derivatives regulation and state gambling law are colliding.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The industry's biggest regulatory risk is becoming jurisdictional fragmentation. A platform cannot scale nationally if federal authorization still leaves it exposed to enforcement in individual states.

1⃣6⃣ The federal government and CFTC sued Arkansas over prediction markets

The U.S. government and CFTC filed a federal case seeking to prevent Arkansas from enforcing state gambling laws against Kalshi.

The case argues that federally regulated event contracts fall under CFTC jurisdiction.

🖊️ Market significance: Federal authorities are now directly challenging state attempts to regulate federally supervised prediction markets.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The prediction-market battle has moved beyond individual companies. It is becoming a direct contest between federal derivatives authority and state gambling powers, and the court decisions could define the industry's U.S. structure.

1⃣7⃣ Kalshi reportedly discussed another funding round at a $65B valuation

Kalshi is reportedly exploring additional financing at a valuation near $65B, shortly after raising $1B at approximately $40B.

The discussions are partly linked to expansion into new markets such as compute futures tied to GPU and cloud-computing prices.

🖊️ Market significance: Investors increasingly view Kalshi as a broader financial exchange rather than solely a prediction-market operator.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A $65B valuation assumes Kalshi becomes much more than an event-contract platform. Compute futures are evidence of that ambition, but the valuation leaves little room for regulatory or execution mistakes.

1⃣8⃣ New York tightened advertising expectations for crypto firms

The New York Department of Financial Services issued new standards requiring regulated crypto companies to establish stronger governance and review processes around marketing.

Firms are expected to communicate fees and risks clearly and avoid misleading claims such as advertising products as free while other charges remain.

Implementation is expected by May 10, 2027.

🖊️ Market significance: Crypto regulation is increasingly extending beyond custody and AML toward the way financial products are marketed to consumers.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is another sign that crypto is being absorbed into ordinary financial regulation. The industry is moving from debating whether rules apply to debating exactly how conventional consumer-protection standards should apply.

1⃣9⃣ BTCS sold ETH below cost to defend an Aave loan

Ethereum treasury company BTCS has reportedly been selling ETH below its acquisition cost to reduce risk surrounding a $64.1M Aave loan.

Approximately 46,676 ETH worth $99.3M backed the debt as of November 9.

Secondary estimates placed its health factor near 1.24 and potential liquidation region around $1,700-$1,717 ETH.

🖊️ Market significance: Falling ETH prices are beginning to expose leverage embedded in corporate digital-asset treasury strategies.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is one of the clearest examples of why treasury yield is not free. Once a corporate ETH position is leveraged through DeFi, falling prices can force asset sales precisely when management would prefer to hold.

2⃣0⃣ Nakamoto extended part of its $165M Bitcoin-backed Kraken loan

Bitcoin treasury company Nakamoto extended a $60M loan tranche originally due in December 2026 until December 2027.

Another $105M remains due in June 2027.

The company has approximately 3,030 BTC pledged as collateral and previously sold around 600 BTC while restructuring the facility.

🖊️ Market significance: Falling Bitcoin prices are reducing the collateral cushion supporting leveraged corporate treasury strategies.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The risk in Bitcoin treasury companies is increasingly moving from asset volatility to financing structure. A company can remain bullish on Bitcoin while still being forced to restructure because its debt matures before the market recovers.

2⃣1⃣ Gemini's trading business contracted sharply in Q3

Gemini reported third-quarter revenue of approximately $40.9M, down 19% year-over-year.

Trading volume fell from $16.4B to $4.5B, a decline of around 73%.

Net loss improved to approximately $58.6M, while adjusted EBITDA remained negative.

🖊️ Market significance: Lower exchange volumes continue pressuring crypto trading businesses even as companies diversify toward services and interest income.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The important number is the 73% collapse in trading volume. Gemini's shift toward recurring services may improve resilience, but the core exchange business is clearly operating in a much weaker demand environment.

2⃣2⃣ Tether's disclosed U.S. equity exposure was estimated around $4.8B

An analysis of public filings estimated that Tether-linked entities hold approximately $4.8B across 13 U.S.-listed companies.

Large exposures include Twenty One Capital, Rumble and Adecoagro, alongside investments in mining, infrastructure and other businesses.

The filings do not establish that these equity positions back USDT reserves.

🖊️ Market significance: Tether is increasingly functioning not only as a stablecoin issuer but as a large strategic capital allocator across crypto and traditional industries.

🗨️ My viewpoint: I would keep these investments separate from USDT reserve analysis unless the company explicitly identifies them as backing assets. The more interesting story is how stablecoin economics are creating one of the largest private investment pools in crypto.

2⃣3⃣ Aave considered reserve-factor changes across 54 assets

Aave governance is considering changes affecting 54 assets across 12 V3 deployments and Ethereum V2.

At recent balances and rates, the changes would increase estimated annualized DAO revenue by approximately $3.5M and raise the blended reserve factor from roughly 12.0% to 12.7%.

🖊️ Market significance: The proposal would redirect a larger share of borrower interest toward the protocol treasury, potentially reducing supplier yields.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is a straightforward economic decision: more protocol revenue versus more attractive depositor yields. The correct balance depends on whether Aave can increase its take rate without pushing liquidity toward competitors.

2⃣4⃣ AKT went live on Solana as Akash began its migration from Cosmos

Akash's AKT token became available on Solana through a 1:1 migration portal that will remain open for two years.

The token can now trade and interact through Solana applications including Jupiter and Raydium.

The underlying Akash compute marketplace has not yet completed its own migration.

🖊️ Market significance: The move expands AKT's liquidity and distribution while demonstrating continued migration of applications and assets toward higher-activity ecosystems.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The token migration matters less than whether Akash eventually moves actual compute activity. Liquidity can migrate quickly; application demand and infrastructure are harder to move.

2⃣5⃣ Injective opened voting for its Veyra upgrade

Injective began governance voting on its v1.21.0 Veyra mainnet upgrade.

The upgrade focuses on institutional real-world-asset infrastructure and cross-chain trading.

If approved, activation is targeted around November 24.

🖊️ Market significance: Injective continues positioning its network toward institutional trading and tokenized financial assets.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The RWA narrative is increasingly crowded, so infrastructure claims alone will not differentiate a network. I would judge Veyra by the assets, institutions and actual trading activity it attracts after launch.

2⃣6⃣ Lightning Labs launched Bitcoin payments for autonomous AI agents

Lightning Labs introduced pi402, an open-source system allowing AI agents to purchase model inference using Bitcoin over the Lightning Network.

The system uses HTTP-402 and Lightning's L402 architecture, allowing agents to pay without conventional accounts, payment cards or API keys.

Spending limits can be programmed directly into the agent.

🖊️ Market significance: Machine-to-machine payments represent a practical use case for programmable, low-value and automated Bitcoin settlement.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is one of the cleaner AI-plus-crypto use cases I have seen. The value is not speculation around AI tokens; it is giving autonomous software a native way to buy the computing resources it needs.

2⃣7⃣ Tokenized-stock liquidity providers are struggling to make money

Research covering 656 tokenized-equity liquidity pools across five blockchains found approximately $7.8B of trading volume and $7.3M of generated fees.

However, liquidity providers suffered approximately $9.65M of impermanent loss.

Even after roughly $1.67M in token incentives, the group remained approximately $680K underwater.

🖊️ Market significance: High tokenized-equity trading volume does not necessarily translate into sustainable economics for the liquidity providers supporting those markets.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is a useful reality check for tokenized stocks. Trading volume can look impressive while the underlying liquidity economics remain broken. Markets cannot scale sustainably if LPs require constant subsidies to stay profitable.

2⃣8⃣ Tokenized Nvidia products showed major price divergence while U.S. markets were closed

Research found that one tokenized Nvidia product traded approximately 8% above four competing Nvidia tokens for around 4.5 hours during a weekend news event.

The widest short-duration discrepancy reached approximately 13%.

The gap was linked to thin liquidity and localized demand and disappeared once additional supply entered the market.

🖊️ Market significance: Twenty-four-hour tokenized-equity trading can create price discovery when traditional markets are closed, but fragmented liquidity can produce substantial deviations between products referencing the same underlying stock.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Continuous trading is only useful if continuous pricing is credible. Tokenized equities need deeper liquidity and stronger arbitrage mechanisms before a weekend token price can reliably be treated as the market price of the underlying stock.

🗨️ My Overall Viewpoint:
Bitcoin's break below $70K, roughly $1.47B of liquidations, six consecutive sessions of BTC and ETH ETF outflows and continued stablecoin contraction show that the weakness is now affecting price, leverage and liquidity simultaneously.

The more concerning development is beginning to appear on balance sheets. BTCS is selling ETH to protect leveraged debt, while Nakamoto is extending Bitcoin-backed financing as collateral values fall. These are early examples of how sustained price weakness can move from market volatility into corporate financing stress.

Meanwhile, Binance's asset replacement, law-enforcement recovery infrastructure and continued institutional development across payments, DeFi and tokenization show that the underlying financial infrastructure continues to mature.

I remain defensive. The immediate test is PPI with the 10-year above 5%, followed by ETF flows and whether Bitcoin can recover $70K. Until liquidity improves and institutional selling slows, I would treat rebounds as tactical rather than evidence of a durable bottom.

After Trump Said “Do What You Have to Do,” Bukele’s Salvadoran Troops Help Strike Gang That Kidnapped 16 American Christian Missionaries | Antonio Graceffo, The Gateway Pundit

Nayib Bukele, the president of El Salvador and an ally of President Trump, is the Latin American leader who locked up his country’s gangs. Since declaring a state of exception in March 2022, his government has detained more than 90,000 people accused of gang ties and built a 40,000-inmate prison, the Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT).

El Salvador’s homicide rate fell from 106 per 100,000 people in 2015 to 1.3 in 2025. At the White House in April 2025, Trump said Bukele had “done a fantastic job,” and Bukele said, “we actually turned the murder capital of the world into the safest country in the Western Hemisphere.”

Bukele has repeatedly criticized Mexico’s failure to defeat its cartels. Speaking to business leaders from more than 20 Latin American countries in February 2025, he said criminal groups “control large sectors of Mexico, Colombia and Brazil” and that “the state is stronger than any criminal organization.”

This month, he told Belizean broadcaster Love FM, “There is no government that cannot eliminate crime.” Haiti is now testing that claim.

Haitian police, backed by Salvadoran troops, struck the headquarters of the 400 Mawozo gang in Croix-des-Bouquets, east of Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince. Bukele announced the strike on X on Nov. 10, saying it also destroyed the home of gang leader Wilson Joseph, known as “Lanmo San Jou.” A Haitian National Police drone task force carried out the attack, which may have killed as many as 20 gunmen. Joseph was away when the strike hit.

On Oct. 16, 2021, 400 Mawozo kidnapped 17 missionaries working for Christian Aid Ministries, an Ohio-based church organization. Sixteen were Americans, one was Canadian, and five were children. The gang demanded $1 million per hostage, and Joseph threatened to kill them if the gang’s demands went unmet. The last hostages regained their freedom after 61 days.

In 2022, the Justice Department charged Joseph with hostage-taking in connection with the kidnapping. Prosecutors said 400 Mawozo claimed responsibility and sought the release of another gang leader, Joly Germine, known as “Yonyon,” who directed the kidnapping from a Haitian prison. The State Department offered a $1 million reward for information leading to Joseph’s arrest. He remains on the FBI’s wanted list.

El Salvador expanded its deployment after an Oct. 18 ambush in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets. Gunmen opened fire on an armored vehicle carrying four Salvadoran aviation technicians attached to the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), the UN-backed multinational force fighting gangs in Haiti. Haitian police later found the burned vehicle in Santo. The four men remain missing.

Bukele warned the gangs, “We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too.” He sent more than 2,000 troops along with military hardware. UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said about 200 Salvadoran troops fall under GSF command. The rest operate under El Salvador’s agreement with the Haitian government.

Bukele discussed the operation by phone with President Trump. Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Oct. 31, Trump recounted the call. “He said that he has a big problem with Haiti. They killed some of his people. I said, ‘You’re running your country. You have to do what you have to do,’” Trump said.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed the exchange on Nov. 8 at Homestead Air Reserve Base in Florida. “He called the President and made them aware of what he was doing, and the President understood why he was doing it,” Rubio said, according to the State Department transcript. Rubio said El Salvador undertook the operation “bilaterally in agreement with the Haitian officials, to go after the gangs that kidnapped their forces.” He added, “We don’t have troops there, but we’ve been engaged.” Rubio said Salvadoran troops and the GSF needed to coordinate to avoid mistaking each other for gang members.

Axios reported on Nov. 10 that David Howell, the U.S. chargé d’affaires in Haiti, told Haitian officials Salvadoran operations should stop “as soon as possible … until they coordinate” with the GSF. “They are going to kill [GSF] troops or civilians,” he warned.

The U.S. Embassy also filed a diplomatic protest alleging that Salvadoran gunfire struck the embassy during an Oct. 31 gang attack on a Salvadoran convoy. El Salvador’s government rejected the allegation and said its soldiers fired away from the embassy. A source who spoke with Bukele told Axios that Bukele responded, “I checked with Trump. He said do what we have to do,” and asked why “some bureaucrat is fighting this?”

Since the Salvadoran deployment expanded, Joseph has written to the UN secretary-general asking for dialogue and citing concern about civilian deaths. He proposed Nov. 18 as a start date for negotiations. Amnesty International’s Americas director, Ana Piquer, called on both governments to publish the deployment agreement. Dominican President Luis Abinader said his government is providing Bukele with logistical and intelligence support.

After the strike, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked Bukele on X, writing, “Hats off to President Nayib Bukele for his support and commitment to the national effort against gangs.” He added, “Haiti, Salvador, FRG: the same fight, the same determination!” FRG is the French abbreviation for the Gang Suppression Force. Fils-Aimé also credited the Haitian National Police and the Armed Forces of Haiti and said the collaboration would continue.

Fils-Aimé is scheduled to visit El Salvador next week to discuss the future of the deployment. In a Nov. 3 post on X addressed to Haitians, Bukele wrote, “We can help you defeat them, but we are not your enemies.” He closed with “Haiti will be free.”

# Learning to Invest in U.S. Stocks from Scratch: Is an S&P 500 ETF Worth Considering? An In-depth Look at Opportunities, Risks, and Long-term Investment Strategies

In the U.S. stock market, many beginners often hope to achieve quick gains by hunting for the "next hot stock." However, the true test in the investment world is not one's ability to make short-term predictions, but rather one's understanding of risk, valuation, and long-term growth.

For those just starting their journey in the U.S. stock market, an S&P 500 ETF—such as VOO—is an investment vehicle worth exploring.

## I. What is VOO, and Why Is It Worth Considering?

VOO is an S&P 500 ETF issued by Vanguard, designed to track the overall performance of large, publicly traded U.S. companies.

It spans a wide range of sectors, including technology, finance, healthcare, and consumer goods. By investing in this single ETF, you gain indirect exposure to a broad basket of major American corporations.

Compared to purchasing shares of individual companies, an index ETF helps mitigate the risks associated with any single stock and spares investors the challenge of selecting specific companies.

## II. Three Key Advantages of Investing in VOO

**1. Diversification of Risk**

VOO covers approximately 500 large U.S. companies. If one company faces operational difficulties, the impact on your overall portfolio is generally much smaller than it would be if you held that company’s stock alone.

However, it is important to note that while diversification reduces the risk of holding individual stocks, it does not protect against a broad market downturn.

**2. Participation in the Long-term Growth of the U.S. Economy**

The United States boasts a mature capital market and numerous companies with strong global competitiveness. Through index investing, you can share in the growth and success of these major enterprises.

**3. Well-Suited for Long-term Investment**

Compared to frequent trading of individual stocks, long-term index investing reduces transaction frequency and the likelihood of making emotionally driven decisions—making it an ideal approach for those looking to build a long-term investment plan.

## III. What Risks Should You Be Aware of When Investing in VOO?

No investment is entirely free of risk.

First, systemic market risk cannot be ignored. In the event of a U.S. economic recession, shifts in interest rates, or a deterioration in market sentiment, the S&P 500 index may experience a significant pullback.

Second, the index has a heavy weighting in the technology sector. If major tech stocks decline simultaneously, the index could be substantially affected.

Finally, valuation risk is also a critical factor to consider. If investors commit large sums of capital when market valuations are excessively high, future returns may be suppressed.

Therefore, one should not assume that VOO’s strong historical performance guarantees continued gains in the future.

## IV. What investment skills should beginners master?

In my view, beginners should focus on four key areas:

First, invest in stages (dollar-cost averaging). Avoid deploying all your capital at a single point in time to mitigate the impact of poor market timing.

Second, manage position sizes. Do not invest money needed for essential living expenses, and exercise caution when using leverage.

Third, take a long-term perspective. Focus on factors like corporate earnings, economic growth, interest rates, and market valuations, rather than obsessing over daily stock price fluctuations.

Fourth, conduct regular reviews. Check whether your portfolio is overly concentrated and ensure it remains aligned with your personal risk tolerance.

## V. Where do future investment opportunities lie?

With the ongoing evolution of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, medical technology, and automation, large U.S. corporations continue to have significant opportunities for innovation.

However, a promising industry outlook does not mean that every related stock is worth buying at a high price.

For investors, it is more important to assess whether a company’s earnings growth can justify its current valuation, and to adjust investment strategies in response to changing market conditions.

## Conclusion: The first step in investing is not making money, but learning to manage risk.

While VOO offers a way to participate in the overall growth of large U.S. companies, it cannot eliminate market risk.

For beginners, developing a sound investment philosophy, understanding asset allocation, managing risk, and maintaining independent judgment are far more important than chasing short-term, outsized gains.

**Truly mature investors do not spend their days hunting for the fastest-rising stocks; instead, they understand why they are investing, what risks they are taking, and how to navigate market volatility.**

Investing is a process of long-term accumulation. By remaining patient, respecting the market, and practicing effective risk management, you position yourself to travel further and more steadily on your long-term investment journey. Click here to get in touch with me:
