$DGXX Q3 2026 earnings: Digi Power X AI sales jump, but 2027 spending climbs

Digi Power X, a former Bitcoin miner building AI data centers, generated nearly half its sales from AI while its operating profit stayed thin. Revenue rose 85% from last quarter to $12.25 million as AI services reached $5.66 million, though total sales landed 8% below chief executive Michel Amar's call target to more than double Q2 revenue by our math. Net income of $1 million relied on crypto and warrant gains, while heavy equipment depreciation kept gross margin negative.

• Revenue: $𝟏𝟐.𝟐𝟓𝐌 (+50% from a year ago (+85% from Q2))
• AI share of revenue: 𝟒𝟔% (16% last quarter and 0% a year ago)
• EBITDA, excluding one-offs: $𝟎.𝟔𝐌 (-$1.0M a year ago)
• Q3 2027 revenue run-rate outlook: 𝐔𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐝 ($250–300M annualized ($143M supported))

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because the company kept its December 15 Alabama delivery date on schedule and secured a $200 million loan commitment arranged by Goldman Sachs. Closing that loan in the fourth quarter would fund Phase 2 of the Cerebras contract without repeating the heavy share sales of the past year. One caution: management unveiled a $350 million capital spending plan for 2027 that exceeds its cash and the proposed loan by about $55 million, by our math.

The question now is whether Digi Power X can fund and contract the rest of its 2027 expansion without diluting shareholders further. Either customer prepayments and the new loan cover the buildout, or the company must tap its share-sale program again while half of its $250 million to $300 million revenue target still lacks a signed tenant. Closing the $200 million credit facility before year-end and delivering Alabama Phase 1 on December 15 will provide the first test.

[Model: Gemini 4 Argon. Full article with charts - link in bio]

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐀𝐈 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐰 𝐆𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐥𝐲 𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐟 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞
"Our third-quarter results demonstrate that Digi Power X’s transformation into an AI infrastructure company is beginning to take hold," chief executive Michel Amar said. The former cryptocurrency miner is replacing its old Bitcoin business with data centers and graphics processing units (GPUs, the specialized chips that run artificial intelligence).

Total revenue rose 85% from last quarter to $12.25 million, and AI services more than quintupled to $5.66 million, or 46.2% of the total. That fell 7.6% short of Amar's call target to more than double Q2 revenue, by our math, but it reversed four straight quarters of year-over-year sales declines.

• Tier III colocation services (renting high-reliability data center space): $3.20 million, up from nil last quarter
• GPU rental on the NeoCloudz platform: $2.46 million, up 127% from $1.08 million last quarter
• Legacy Bitcoin colocation and mining: $3.29 million, down to 26.9% of sales from 63% a year ago

What to watch: the segment footnote in the upcoming third-quarter Form 10-Q filing. It will show whether the $3.20 million of colocation sales came from recurring hosting fees or one-time construction payments ahead of the January billing start.

🟢 𝐀𝐥𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐦𝐚 𝐏𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝟏 𝐇𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐬 𝐈𝐭𝐬 𝐃𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐦𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐞
Digi Power X has a ten-year agreement with AI chipmaker Cerebras to lease up to 40 megawatts (MW, a measure of electrical capacity) at its Columbiana, Alabama campus. After three earlier equipment milestones slipped by one quarter in early 2026, keeping the Alabama schedule is critical because the contract carries penalty and termination clauses for late delivery.

The company confirmed that Phase 1 (15 MW) remains on schedule to give Cerebras access and begin testing liquid-cooling systems on December 15, 2026. Billing starts in January 2027 at $35.1 million a year initially, averaging about $40 million over ten years, while Phase 2 (25 MW) construction is underway for March 2027 access alongside longer-term plans in New York, North Carolina and West Virginia.

What to watch: an announcement confirming Phase 1 commissioning on or before December 15, 2026. On-time delivery unlocks about $8.8 million of quarterly revenue starting in the first quarter of 2027.

🟢 𝐀 $𝟐𝟎𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐋𝐨𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐍𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠
Phase 2 of the Cerebras contract is worth $58.5 million a year, but it is conditioned on Digi Power X securing adequate financing. Until now, management funded construction by selling new stock, which more than tripled the share count between late 2024 and August 2026.

On October 13, the data center operator received a commitment letter from a major lender for $200 million in project debt, arranged by Goldman Sachs, and expects to close it in the fourth quarter. Because a commitment letter is still "subject to definitive documentation and the satisfaction of various conditions, including the lender’s completion of its diligence", the financing risk is fading rather than settled.

What to watch: a filing confirming the signed credit agreement before year-end. Closing the loan removes the main condition blocking Phase 2 and its $58.5 million of annual revenue.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐍𝐞𝐰 $𝟑𝟓𝟎 𝐌𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐬 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐅𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠
Chairman Michel Amar said the group will "fund expansion principally through customer contributions and contract-backed financing" while minimizing dilution. Digi Power X has relied on an at-the-market equity program (which sells newly created shares into the open market) to fund its buildout so far.

For the first time, the release put a price tag on next year's buildout: $350 million of 2027 capital spending for 10 MW of AI chip capacity and Alabama Phase 2. Even if the $200 million loan closes, combining it with $95.1 million of cash on hand (excluding crypto) leaves a $54.9 million gap by our math, before counting fourth-quarter spending.

Shareholders' equity also rose $14.9 million in the third quarter despite only $1.0 million of net income and $2.2 million of stock compensation. By our math, that leaves $11.7 million of unexplained equity increases, indicating that share issuance continued during the quarter.

What to watch: the share count and cash flow statement in the third-quarter Form 10-Q. Further share sales below $4 would consume much of the per-share value of the Alabama contract.

🔴🔴 𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐇𝐚𝐬 𝐍𝐨 𝐒𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫
Digi Power X reiterated its outlook for $250 million to $300 million in annualized revenue by the end of the third quarter of 2027. For the first time, the company published an illustrative table breaking down how much of that target is backed by current operations and the Cerebras contract.

• Current Q3 operations annualized: $49.0 million
• Columbiana Phase 1 (contracted Year 1 rate): $35.1 million
• Columbiana Phase 2 (conditional on financing): $58.5 million
• Total supported run-rate: $142.6 million, leaving $132.4 million uncontracted at the $275 million middle of the range by our math

The company said the remaining $107 million to $157 million must come "from additional AI colocation and GPU capacity currently in development and in customer negotiations". Because its New York sites only begin converting to AI in the third and fourth quarters of 2027, the timeline to build and fill that extra capacity by September 2027 is tight.

What to watch: signed customer contracts with committed minimum payments for the planned 10 MW of GPU capacity before mid-2027. Without them, the company cannot reach its $250 million floor on time.

🔴 𝐄𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐊𝐞𝐩𝐭 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐍𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞
As AI services grew to nearly half of sales, gross profit before depreciation and amortization (the non-cash charge for wearing out equipment) flipped from a $1.46 million loss in Q2 to a $3.08 million profit, or 25.1% of revenue by our math. However, putting $30 million of GPUs and new infrastructure into service drove depreciation in cost of sales up by 25.2 percentage points of revenue from a year ago, to 44.8%.

That non-cash charge left GAAP gross profit at a loss of $2.41 million (-19.7% gross margin, 9.2 percentage points worse than a year ago). Reported net income of $1.0 million relied on $7.1 million of crypto price gains and $1.5 million of warrant revaluation gains; excluding those one-offs, Digi Power X lost $7.6 million by our math, and EBITDA excluding one-offs was just $0.6 million.

What to watch: gross margin after Alabama Phase 1 billing begins in the first quarter of 2027. High-margin colocation fees must cover the rising depreciation bill from the $145.6 million fixed asset base.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
Because the earnings release contained only summary tables rather than full financial statements, three standing concerns from prior filings received no update today.

• Share count and ATM dilution: the release omitted the exact share count and any share sales after August; the Form 10-Q cover page and equity footnote will show the dilution.
• Customer concentration: the release named no new colocation tenant beyond Cerebras and did not update the usage-based GPU contract with investee SubQ; the 10-Q lease footnote will test this.
• Governance and internal controls: the release gave no update on remediating prior material weaknesses in financial reporting or the terms of the West Virginia power letter of intent with a board member's firm.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐓𝐨𝐤𝐞𝐧 𝐅𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐋𝐚𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐀𝐈 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲
"Going live with the NeoCloudz Token Factory is a major step for Digi Power X," president Alec Amar said. Instead of only renting out raw GPU servers at wholesale rates, the new platform uses the company's own power and chips to sell AI inference tokens (the unit of output when an AI model answers a prompt) directly to customers, though the release reported no token sales yet.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐟𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟒𝟓.𝟔 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Property and equipment nearly doubled in a single quarter, rising 99% from $73.24 million in Q2 and 646% from $19.5 million a year ago. The $72.4 million sequential jump reflects rapid construction and equipment installation at the Columbiana, Alabama data center ahead of its December 15 Phase 1 commissioning.

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟏𝟗.𝟔𝟒 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Total liquidity fell 16% from $142.42 million at the end of Q2 as the company paid for Alabama construction, while borrowings stayed at zero. Digital currencies (Bitcoin and Ethereum) made up $24.5 million of the total, up 56% from a year ago, leaving $95.14 million in cash and cash equivalents by our math.

𝐄𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐲 𝐬𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟑.𝟐𝟗 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Power sales to the electrical grid rose 68% from $1.96 million last quarter and 9% from $3.03 million a year ago, accounting for 26.9% of total revenue. The segment provides steady cash flow from the company's New York power assets while it prepares those sites for AI conversion in late 2027.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐐𝟑 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐀𝐧𝐧𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐑𝐮𝐧-𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞: $𝟐𝟓𝟎–𝟑𝟎𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠆 unchanged from $250–300 million
Unchanged. The plan calls for monthly revenue of $21 million to $25 million by September 2027, which implies $68.75 million of quarterly sales at the middle of the range (+461% from Q3 2026 by our math). Current operations and the Cerebras contract (including conditional Phase 2) supply $142.6 million of that annualized pace, leaving $132.4 million to come from uncontracted capacity.

𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬: ~$𝟑𝟓𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
New. Management expects to spend about $350 million next year to build 10 MW of AI token factory capacity and finish Phase 2 at Columbiana. The US group plans to fund the bill through customer prepayments, cash on hand, and contract-backed debt, including the proposed $200 million Goldman Sachs facility.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 $𝟑.𝟐𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐢𝐞𝐫 𝐈𝐈𝐈 𝐜𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞?
Chief executive Michel Amar noted that third-quarter results arrived "all before the expected start of Columbiana colocation billing in January 2027". Investors need to know whether the $3.20 million of colocation sales came from one-time Cerebras construction fees or another customer.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐲 𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐞𝐝 𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐀𝐓𝐌 𝐢𝐧 𝐐𝟑?
Shareholders' equity grew by $14.87 million in Q3, which is $11.67 million more than net income and stock-based compensation combined by our math. The release omitted the share count, leaving unclear how much stock was sold and at what price.

𝐖𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 $𝟓𝟓 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐜𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐱 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦?
Even if the $200 million debt facility closes, combining it with $95.1 million of cash on hand falls $54.9 million short of the $350 million 2027 spending plan by our math. Management has not said how much customer prepayment it has secured.

𝐇𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐢𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐥 𝐰𝐞𝐚𝐤𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓 𝐛𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐝?
In late 2025 the company reported material weaknesses in its financial reporting controls and targeted remediation by the end of 2025. Neither the second-quarter nor the third-quarter release updated investors on whether those controls are now effective.

It is important to remember that a crime committed by an illegal alien is a preventable crime.The following cases may not represent the general illegal alien population, but they demonstrate the value of strong borders and underscore why illegal immigration remains a public safety concern. The information is gathered from various credible news sources and publicly-accessible official sources. The crimes do not include terrorist actions, but deal with crimes of a serious nature, such as homicide or manslaughter, rape or sexual crimes, assault on ors. October 2026
Oscar Baltodano Lopez & Benjamin Santez Lopez (October 1 & 2, 2026)
On October 1, illegal immigrants Oscar Baltodano Lopez and Benjamin Santez Lopez allegedly kidnapped and raped an underage girl in Washington County, Missouri. According to the victim, she was out walking when Baltodano Lopez grabbed her and dragged her into his house. He then proceeded to assault and rape her. Benjamin Santez Lopez allegedly raped her afterward. Sheriff’s deputies identified the house and got a search warrant; however, the suspects refused to comply with their commands. Deputies then entered the house and found Oscar Lopez hiding in a locked bathroom. Deputies took both men into custody and charged them. Shortly after, immigration detainers were lodged against them. It is unknown when or where they entered the country illegally. 
(KRCG 13, October 2026; First Alert 4, October 2026; KSDK 5, October 2026)
Dangelo Rafael Jean Caraballo & Sneider Mejia Bautista (October 2, 2026)
On October 2, Dominican nationals Dangelo Rafael Jean Caraballo and Sneider Mejia Bautista allegedly stabbed an off-duty New York Police Department (NYPD) detective and then fled the scene in the Bronx, New York. According to reports, 33-year-old Detective Jose Mercedes was cleaning out the trunk of his car when the two suspects ambushed him and tried to steal his gold chain. He tried defending himself but was stabbed multiple times in the neck and leg. Caraballo and Bautista then fled the scene on a motorized bike. Mercedes was rushed in an ambulance to a nearby hospital and, since then, has recovered enough to be discharged. The two suspects were later tracked down to a residence in Massachusetts and taken into custody. Following their sentencing, DHS lodged detainers against both men and revealed that they both had extensive criminal records. Caraballo was arrested by U.S. Border Patrol for illegally entering the country in February 2023 but was released into the country. Bautista illegally entered the country in December 2022, and he was issued a final order of removal in May 2025.
(DHS, October 2026; New York Post, October 2026; Fox News, October 2026; CBS News, October 2026)
Emilio Vallejo Ortiz (October 3, 2026)
On October 3, illegal alien Emilio Vallejo Ortiz allegedly murdered his coworker, and possible lover, in Shakopee, Minnesota. Police discovered the body of the 53-year-old victim, who owned a local landscaping company, off a walking trail in a park. After searching the area, police were able to rule the death a homicide after finding a pool of blood and 9mm shell casings. Police then reviewed security camera footage from a nearby Menard’s and located one of the victim’s pickup trucks near Ortiz’s apartment, which Ortiz had borrowed from the victim recently. Investigators concluded that Ortiz was the main suspect. When detectives interviewed Ortiz, his story did not match the available phone and security data, and he later claimed that he didn’t remember the day. After the interview, Ortiz was taken into custody, and authorities lodged a detainer against him. It is unknown when or where he entered the country illegally.
(KROC, October 2026; Fox 9, October 2026; KSTP, October 2026)
Franck Anderson Bazil (October 4, 2026)
On October 4, illegal alien Franck Anderson Bazil allegedly committed a fatal hit-and-run in Indianapolis, Indiana. According to police, 9-year-old Roland McLain III and his 6-year-old brother were playing on the grass in front of an apartment complex when Bazil came around the corner too fast and drove over them. Bazil then fled the scene, but he was arrested a few hours later while waiting in line for a car wash. During the crash, Roland McLain’s head was crushed and unfortunately succumbed to his injuries at a nearby hospital. His brother suffered internal injuries and remains in critical condition. At first, it was believed that Bazil was a U.S. citizen because he possessed a driver’s license and Social Security card. However, during his initial hearing, he required an interpreter, and his attorney said he was not a citizen. Later, ICE lodged a detainer against Bazil and reported that he illegally entered the country in January 2024.
(WIBC, October 2026; Fox 59, October 2026; WTHR, October 2026; WRTV 6, October 2026)
Rudi Lacatusu & Mirabela Lacatusu (October 5, 2026)
On October 5, Romanian nationals of Romani background Rudi Lacatusu and Mirabela Lacatusu were arrested for allegedly running a scheme that stole jewelry across multiple states. The couple, who have been dubbed the ‘Romanian Bonnie and Clyde,’ allegedly carried out 14 robberies across New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, and Maryland. The couple was caught after a 73-year-old victim noticed that her gold necklace was missing in Valley Stream, New York. To commit this act, they drove up to the victim to ask for directions, after which Mirabela exited the vehicle to thank the victim by hugging her. She then took off the gold necklace and replaced it with two gold-colored necklaces, before the two suspects drove off. Investigators connected the Lacatusus to similar robberies in the surrounding area. After their arrest, the two were turned over to ICE custody and are awaiting removal.
(DHS, October 2026; Nassau County Police Department, October 2026; CBS News, October 2026)
Uriel Santiago Perez (October 6, 2026)
On October 6, Mexican national Uriel Santiago Perez allegedly sexually assaulted an underage boy during a house tour in North Fort Myers, Florida. Perez is a transgender man who claims that he is a woman. According to reports, Perez scheduled a tour of the house that was recently listed with the victim’s father. During the tour, he took the underage boy into a bathroom, where he exposed his breasts to the victim and then forcefully sexually assaulted him. After the attack, the father called the police, but Perez left the scene. Police arrested the suspect at the end of the street, where he was waiting for the victim to meet him. Once in custody, ICE lodged a detainer against him. Perez was previously encountered in 2015 but did not meet the Obama administration’s enforcement priorities at the time and never had a detainer lodged against him. 
(Townhall, October 2026; WFLA 8, October 2026; Gulf Coast News Now, October 2026)
Victor Soseia Hachipan (October 7, 2026)
On October 7, Micronesian national Victor Soseia Hachipan was arrested by ICE after being encountered in Keizer, Oregon. Hachipan is a registered sex offender who has been shielded by the sanctuary policies of Oregon since 2021. Hachipan was first convicted of sexually assaulting a victim under 14 years old and a few other crimes in 2021, but officials ignored ICE’s detainer and released him back into the community. In 2023, he was convicted of robbery but was again released. Since then, ICE has attempted to locate Hachipan and finally succeeded in obtaining information on his whereabouts after a federal judge ordered Marion County to comply. With this information, ICE found and apprehended the suspect. Hachipan entered the country at an unknown time and location.
(DHS, October 2026; TVC News, October 2026; Breitbart, October 2026)
Mario Jesus Valdez-Flores (October 7, 2026)
On October 7, Mexican national Mario Jesus Valdez-Flores was arrested by ICE during a traffic stop in Kings Beach, California. Valdez-Flores was previously deported from the United States five times and has an extensive criminal history, which includes selling drugs, robbery, and assault with a deadly weapon. He was lawfully admitted in 2004 but overstayed his authorized period of admission before his multiple deportations. He remains in ICE custody until he is removed to Mexico.
(DHS, October 2026; New York Post, October 2026)
Braulio Daniel Sanchez Orozco (October 8, 2026)
On October 8, illegal alien Braulio Daniel Sanchez Orozco was indicted for murdering and abusing the corpse of his mother in Louisville, Kentucky. Sanchez Orozco allegedly murdered his mother, 44-year-old Maria Elena Sanchez Orozco, and then called 911 to try to cover it up. He was not initially charged and claimed that the victim’s boyfriend was responsible. In July, he was arrested by ICE in Mississippi and later transferred to Kentucky. ICE reported that he entered the country on a temporary basis but overstayed and remained in the country illegally.
(Border Hawk News, October 2026; WLKY, October 2026)
Junior Jose Davila-Moran (October 14, 2026)
On October 14, Guatemalan national Junior Jose Davila-Moran allegedly attempted to kidnap an Amish woman in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. According to investigators and the victim, Davila-Moran allegedly approached her from behind while she was working and held her at knifepoint. He then tried handcuffing her. The 23-year-old victim began to scream and chased the suspect off the property with her weed whacker. Davila-Moran fled the area, but investigators used license-plate readers to identify him and his vehicle. On October 16, investigators showed the victim a photo lineup, and she immediately identified Davila-Moran. He was arrested later that day and charged with several charges, including attempted kidnapping. ICE also lodged a detainer against him and revealed that he illegally entered the country as a juvenile in January 2018. 
(WGAL 8, October 2026; Lancaster Online, October 2026; Fox 17, October 2026; Fox 43, October 2026)
Elmer Jose Cardona Bustillo (October 15, 2026)
On October 15, Honduran national Elmer Jose Cardona Bustillo was allegedly driving illegally when he struck and seriously injured a woman with Down syndrome in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin. According to reports, Bustillo was driving home from work when he struck the 50-year-old victim in the crosswalk. The victim was transported to a local hospital with serious injuries, including a fractured collarbone, facial fractures, and brain bleeding. She had to be airlifted to another hospital, where she is on a ventilator and remains in critical condition. After being taken into custody, he admitted to police that he did not have a driver’s license and did not see the victim. ICE later lodged a detainer against him and revealed that he illegally entered the country at an unknown time but was issued a final order of removal in November 2015.
(WRPN, October 2026; WBay, October 2026; WISN 12, October 2026)
Yostin Valentin Lopez Gomez (October 15, 2026)
On October 15, illegal alien Yostin Valentin Lopez Gomez allegedly murdered a man outside of his apartment in Gwinnett County, Georgia. According to detectives, Yostin Valentin Lopez Gomez drove himself and other suspects to the victim’s, 21-year-old Luis Mario Munoz Ortiz, apartment, where they shot him twice. When police were called to investigate the reported gunfire, they found the victim unresponsive and pronounced him dead at the scene. Investigators determined that Yostin Valentin Lopez Gomez was the main suspect by using Flock license plate readers to identify and track his vehicle. It is believed that the shooting is related to a drug-related dispute. Lopez Gomez currently has an immigration detainer hold.
(11 Alive, October 2026; Fox 5, October 2026; Atlanta News First, October 2026)
Guillermo Carmona-Lopez (October 16, 2026)
On October 16, Mexican national Guillermo Carmona-Lopez allegedly caused a fatal car crash in North Haven, Connecticut. According to the police, Carmona-Lopez was driving the wrong way on Interstate 91 when he struck 21-year-old Ryan O’Shea’s car head-on. O’Shea’s car was sent into another lane where it was struck by two more vehicles. When police and paramedics arrived at the scene, O’Shea was pronounced dead, and Carmona-Lopez was transported to a nearby hospital with life-threatening injuries. At some point, investigators uncovered that Carmona-Lopez is in the country illegally, and DHS reported that he had illegally entered the country numerous times and was issued a final order of removal in May 2013. He reentered again at an unknown time and place. Carmona-Lopez’s victim, Ryan O’Shea, was a well-respected student at the University of New Hampshire, where he was the captain of the club hockey team, president of a fraternity, and active in the community. O’Shea was set to graduate in Spring 2027 with a degree in Criminal Justice, and his dream was to be an officer with the New York Police Department (NYPD).
(WFSB 3, October 2026; WHMI 93.5 FM, October 2026; Fox News, October 2026)
Ezequiel Hernandez (October 19, 2026)
On October 19, illegal alien Ezequiel Hernandez allegedly shot and killed a man in Garland, Texas. According to police, Hernandez and the victim had an argument inside a business, which later escalated into the shooting. When police and paramedics arrived at the scene, the victim was pronounced dead. The victim’s brother claims the argument was over a game of pool. Hernandez then fled the scene but was tracked down and taken into custody by police. After being charged with murder, an immigration hold was placed on him. It is unknown when or where he illegally entered the country. 
(Dallas County Mugshots, October 2026; CBS News, October 2026; Fox 4, October 2026; NBC 5, October 2026)
Destino Jean-Louis (October 21, 2026)
On October 21, Haitian national Destino Jean-Louis allegedly murdered his wife outside of a Walmart in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Police responded to the store to investigate reported gunshots and found the body of 45-year-old Latosha Ann Cooper with a bullet wound to the head. She was pronounced dead at the scene. Using security camera footage, investigators identified Jean-Louis. On October 23, the U.S. Marshals arrested Jean-Louis and charged him with first-degree and third-degree murder. Jean-Louis entered the country through the CHNV program in November 2023. He and the victim began dating a few months later and were married in March 2025. According to coworkers, Jean-Louis was using Cooper to get immigration status. However, the couple broke up, and she withdrew the green card application, which caused Jean-Louis to lose status. This upset him, and he began calling the store regularly in the months leading up to the murder to ask about Cooper’s work schedule. He is still under investigation.

Is the AI bubble actually deflating, or is the market simply becoming more realistic about AI valuations?

Anthropic’s upcoming IPO is an interesting case to watch.

A few weeks ago, reports suggested that Anthropic could be targeting a valuation of around $2 trillion. But following the recent tech market selloff, some investors reportedly reconsidered that valuation, with discussions falling toward the $1.1T–$1.3T range.

There was also an initial reported IPO price range of $70–$80, which was later retracted. Subsequent reports discussed an updated $70–$78 range.

These figures come from different stages of reporting, so they shouldn’t be treated as one confirmed set of final IPO terms.

So, is this the beginning of an AI bubble deflating?

I think it’s more interesting to look at this as a possible shift in market expectations.

AI is still developing, and companies like Anthropic have real products and growing demand. But having strong technology doesn’t automatically justify any valuation.

Investors may be starting to look beyond the AI hype and pay closer attention to actual business performance, revenue, competition, infrastructure costs, and how long it might take for these companies to become profitable.

For traders, this is a reminder that market sentiment can change quickly. A company can have strong long-term potential while its valuation still gets reassessed.

Where does Bitget come in?

For those interested in exploring Anthropic-related exposure, Bitget offers access through its IPO Prime Public Round.

Users can subscribe using USDT or USDGO, subject to eligibility and the applicable subscription rules. After allocation, participants receive rANT, a token that provides tokenized exposure to Anthropic.

Bitget provides access to this tokenized product. It is not Anthropic’s IPO underwriter and is not affiliated with Anthropic.

My personal takeaway here is that maybe the bigger story isn’t whether AI is losing its potential, but whether the market is finally becoming more selective about the price it puts on that potential.

Do you think this is a healthy valuation reset for the AI industry, or a sign that the AI hype is starting to cool down?

text:
THE PRICE OF TURNING AGAINST ISRAEL: WHAT THE STUDENT LIST'S FOREIGN POLICY COULD MEAN FOR SERBIA

PART II — Defence, Strategic Consequences, Bosnia's Historical Record and the Cost of Political Ideology

A PROMISE TO STOP SOMETHING IS NOT A PLAN TO GOVERN

In Part I, I examined Filip Ubović's declaration that a future government led by the Student List would stop arms trade with Israel and terminate the Serbian-Israeli drone manufacturing project. I also examined the economic interests, industrial opportunities and strategic relationship that such a decision could put at risk.

But there is a larger question that deserves attention.

What happens if the Student List actually comes to power and attempts to implement this policy?

It is one thing to announce a position during a political campaign. It is another to take responsibility for the consequences of turning that position into government policy.

The Student List is not proposing a minor adjustment to Serbia's diplomatic language. Its representative has described an intention to stop an existing defence relationship with a technologically advanced country, disrupt an industrial project and change the direction of Serbia's cooperation with Israel.

That has implications for the Serbian Armed Forces, domestic defence manufacturers, international suppliers, investors, workers and the country's diplomatic position.

And yet, where is the detailed plan?

Where is the assessment of existing military contracts? Where is the replacement strategy? Where is the explanation of how Serbia will maintain equipment already purchased, protect its industrial interests and avoid unnecessary financial and operational disruption?

A political movement that wants to govern a country cannot simply identify what it dislikes. It must explain what it intends to do instead.

This is where the Student List's position becomes particularly difficult to defend.

It is proposing to dismantle a relationship without demonstrating that Serbia would be stronger, safer or economically better off afterwards.

THE FIRST CONSEQUENCE: SERBIA COULD WEAKEN ITS OWN DEFENCE CAPABILITIES

Serbia's military modernisation has involved cooperation with several international suppliers. Israeli defence technology is one part of that wider programme.

The relationship with Elbit Systems is particularly significant because it extends beyond the purchase of equipment.

Reporting in 2026 described a series of Serbian procurement arrangements involving Israeli systems, including PULS artillery systems, Hermes unmanned aircraft, precision weapons and electronic-warfare capabilities. The drone manufacturing initiative was intended to take cooperation further, moving beyond the simple purchase of finished foreign equipment towards local assembly and production.

That distinction is important.

When a country purchases a complete military system from abroad, it remains dependent on the supplier for varying degrees of technical support, spare parts, maintenance, upgrades and future integration.

When it develops domestic production and servicing capacity, it has the opportunity to reduce some of that dependence.

It does not automatically achieve technological independence. That depends on the contractual arrangements, access to intellectual property, local component production, training and the degree of control retained by the domestic partner.

But it creates a pathway that would otherwise require years of independent investment and development.

If Serbia terminates cooperation with Israel, it will have to consider what happens to systems already acquired and what replaces the future capabilities that the partnership was intended to provide.

This is not a theoretical concern.

Modern military equipment is not interchangeable simply because two products perform broadly similar functions. Different systems require different training, communications architecture, maintenance arrangements, ammunition, software, logistics and operational integration.

Replacing one supplier with another can involve substantial transition costs.

A responsible government would first conduct a detailed audit of every relevant contract, delivery schedule, support obligation and operational requirement. It would then determine whether termination is legally possible, financially justified and militarily sensible.

The Student List has not publicly demonstrated that it has completed such an assessment.

Its position appears to begin with the desired political outcome and leave the military consequences for somebody else to resolve.

That is not how a serious defence policy is developed.

THE SECOND CONSEQUENCE: SERBIA WILL LOSE AN OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP ITS OWN DEFENCE INDUSTRY

Serbia has an established defence-industrial tradition. Its companies have manufactured ammunition, artillery systems, small arms, vehicles and other military equipment for decades.

The next stage of development requires more than increasing the quantity of traditional products.

Modern warfare increasingly depends on unmanned aircraft, electronic systems, advanced sensors, communications, software, precision weapons and the integration of multiple platforms.

This is an area where international partnerships can make a difference.

Cooperation with an established Israeli defence manufacturer offers Serbia an opportunity to develop experience in a technological field where Israel has significant international expertise.

The important question is how much of that expertise can become embedded in Serbia's domestic industrial base.

Will Serbian engineers receive advanced training? Will local companies manufacture components? Will maintenance and repair capabilities be established domestically? Will Serbian personnel be able to operate and service the systems without permanent dependence on foreign technicians? Will Serbia obtain meaningful rights to manufacture and export products?

These are the questions the Serbian government should be asking Elbit and any other international partner.

They are also the questions the Student List should answer before proposing to end the relationship.

The argument is not that every foreign defence partnership is automatically beneficial. Nor should Serbia accept arrangements that leave it with little control over production, technology or intellectual property.

The argument is that Serbia should negotiate to obtain more from its partnerships, not casually abandon them.

If the current arrangements are insufficient, improve them.

If Serbian ownership and control are inadequate, renegotiate them.

If domestic suppliers are being excluded, demand greater local participation.

If the technology transfer is too limited, make that a condition of future cooperation.

There is a substantial difference between demanding better terms and terminating a strategic industrial opportunity.

The Student List should explain why it believes the second option serves Serbia better than the first.

THE THIRD CONSEQUENCE: A GOVERNMENT THAT CANCELS AGREEMENTS MUST ACCEPT THE BILL

There is a financial dimension to this issue that cannot be avoided.

A new government can review decisions made by its predecessor. It can investigate contracts, renegotiate arrangements and change procurement priorities.

But it cannot simply pretend that existing agreements disappear when political leadership changes.

A termination decision would require a review of the relevant contractual provisions, including:

Outstanding payments and financial commitments.

Equipment already delivered or under production.

Termination and compensation clauses.

Guarantees and financial security arrangements.

Maintenance, servicing and technical-support obligations.

Ownership of equipment, facilities and intellectual property.

Rights relating to manufacturing, licensing and exports.

Obligations involving subcontractors and other suppliers.

The actual financial consequences would depend on the individual contracts. The face value of a procurement agreement is not automatically the amount payable if it is cancelled. Equally, cancellation is not automatically free.

There could be direct termination costs, replacement procurement expenses, additional training requirements and operational delays.

There could also be consequences that are harder to calculate, including lost industrial opportunities and reduced confidence among potential international partners.

The Serbian taxpayer would ultimately carry the burden of any public financial consequences.

This is why the Student List should publish a serious policy assessment rather than rely on a moral declaration.

If it believes Serbia should terminate the agreements, it should explain the estimated cost, the legal mechanism, the replacement equipment and the expected effect on the country's defence readiness.

It should also explain how it intends to compensate for the loss of industrial and technological cooperation.

Until those questions are answered, the proposal remains an intention without a demonstrated national-interest case.

THE FOURTH CONSEQUENCE: SERBIA'S INTERNATIONAL CREDIBILITY WILL  SUFFER

There is another cost that should not be underestimated.

International partnerships depend on trust and predictability.

Defence agreements are often developed over several years. They involve substantial capital, technical planning, production schedules, training and long-term support. Companies make decisions based on their expectation that the contractual and regulatory environment will remain sufficiently stable to justify investment.

A government is entitled to review agreements that do not serve its country. That is part of democratic accountability.

But a government that cancels strategic projects primarily to satisfy a political position, without demonstrating a legal or economic justification, risks creating uncertainty for future investors.

An international company considering a defence or technology project in Serbia will inevitably ask whether an agreement signed with one administration can be relied upon after a change of government.

That concern would not be limited to Israeli companies.

It could affect other potential partners considering investments in advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity, electronics, research and defence technology.

Serbia wants to attract investment and strengthen its industrial capabilities. It cannot simultaneously promote itself as a reliable destination for long-term industrial partnerships while treating strategically important projects as disposable political symbols.

This does not mean foreign investors should be allowed to dictate Serbian policy.

Quite the opposite.

Serbia must have the confidence to negotiate firmly, protect its domestic interests and enforce its laws. But there is a difference between sovereign oversight and political unpredictability.

A sovereign country chooses its partners. It does not allow domestic political movements to turn every international relationship into an ideological loyalty test.

THE OWNERSHIP QUESTION: TRANSPARENCY IS ESSENTIAL, BUT IT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR POLITICAL SABOTAGE

The drone project also raises legitimate questions about corporate ownership and governance.

Investigative reporting by BIRN raised questions about the registered corporate structure behind the Makiš assembly facility and the difference between the ownership arrangements publicly described by Serbian officials and the corporate records available at the time.

The appointment of Israeli lawyer Zion Amir, who has represented Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as a director of the company operating the facility also attracted attention.

These questions deserve proper answers.

Who ultimately owns the operating company? What is the precise relationship between the company and Elbit Systems? What is Yugoimport-SDPR's legal and commercial position? Who controls the production process? What is the division of responsibilities? Who owns the intellectual property? What happens to the products and facilities if the partnership ends?

The Serbian public should not be expected to accept vague assurances about a strategic industrial project.

A proper parliamentary and regulatory examination would be entirely reasonable.

But this is precisely where the Student List's argument becomes inadequate.

If the ownership arrangements are problematic, investigate them.

If the Serbian state has failed to secure sufficient control, establish why.

If the agreement does not adequately protect domestic interests, renegotiate it.

If there has been misconduct, pursue accountability.

None of those actions requires an automatic abandonment of the relationship with Israel.

The national interest should be the standard by which the project is evaluated, not the political convenience of the moment.

BOSNIA: THE FOREIGN FIGHTERS WHO FOUGHT ALONGSIDE BOSNIAN MUSLIM FORCES

The Student List's position on Israel also raises a wider question about historical memory and the consistency of its humanitarian arguments.

If a political movement wants to place the suffering of Palestinians at the centre of its foreign-policy declarations, it should be prepared to examine the historical record of other conflicts in which international religious and political networks became involved.

For Serbia, one of the most important examples is the Bosnian war.

Between 1992 and 1995, Bosnia and Herzegovina became a destination for foreign Islamist fighters who travelled from countries across the Muslim world to participate in the conflict.

These men were commonly referred to as the Mujahedin.

Their presence was not simply a matter of humanitarian assistance. Some foreign volunteers initially arrived through humanitarian organisations, but international judicial proceedings established that many subsequently became involved in combat alongside the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia examined this history in considerable detail in the case of Rasim Delić, the former commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The ICTY judgment explains that the first foreign Mujahedin arrived in central Bosnia during 1992, entering largely through Croatia. It also describes the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment on 13 August 1993, following an order signed by Delić.

The foreign fighters were principally from the Arab world and other Muslim-majority countries. They were organised into a formation that became associated with the Bosnian Army's Third Corps.

The tribunal examined their involvement in the conflict and crimes committed against captured soldiers.

On 15 September 2008, Rasim Delić was sentenced to three years' imprisonment after being found responsible for failing to take necessary and reasonable measures to prevent and punish cruel treatment committed by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment against captured Bosnian Serb soldiers at Livade and Kamenica Camp in July and August 1995.

This is a particularly important part of the historical record.

The crimes against Bosnian Serb prisoners were not simply allegations made in the aftermath of the war. They were examined in international criminal proceedings and formed the basis of a conviction.

Serbian victims deserve to have those findings remembered.

Their suffering should not be pushed aside because contemporary political movements find it more convenient to discuss other conflicts.

THE PALESTINIAN CONNECTION IN BOSNIA

There is a specific question that deserves further investigation: Palestinian individuals participation among the foreign fighters who travelled to Bosnia and fought alongside Bosnian Muslim forces.

It is important to distinguish between three separate issues.

The first is the documented presence of foreign Mujahedin in Bosnia. That is established by the ICTY record.

The second is the international character of the networks that supported and recruited foreign fighters. Judicial and historical research describes assistance, recruitment and ideological connections extending across the wider Muslim world.

The publicly available ICTY material examined for this article establishes the Palestine foreign-fighter phenomenon, their participation in combat and crimes war committed against Bosnian Serbs. Palestinian nationals participated as individual volunteers, their involvement is well documented and examined.  The historical record must be treated honestly.

What can be said with confidence is that foreign fighters from the Muslim world including from Palestine travelled to Bosnia, joined formations fighting against Bosnian Serb forces and that members of the El Mujahedin Detachment committed crimes against captured Serb soldiers.

That history deserves attention whenever contemporary political movements invoke religious solidarity, international justice and humanitarian responsibility.

It is legitimate to ask why the suffering of Palestinians is treated as an urgent political concern while the suffering of Bosnian Serbs at the hands of muslim foreign fighters receives so much less attention in the same political conversations.

It is legitimate to demand consistency.

And it is legitimate to insist that the victims of crimes against Serbs are never to be forgotten.

THE MORAL STANDARD CANNOT CHANGE DEPENDING ON WHO THE VICTIM IS

This is the deeper problem with selective humanitarian politics.

The suffering of civilians in Gaza deserves attention. The suffering of Serbian civilians during the Bosnian war deserves attention. The murder and mistreatment of prisoners deserves condemnation regardless of their nationality, religion or political allegiance.

There should be no hierarchy of victims.

If the Student List believes that international humanitarian law must guide Serbian foreign policy, then it should apply that principle consistently.

It should recognise the rights and suffering of Israeli civilians subjected to terrorism. It should acknowledge the suffering of Palestinian civilians. It should also recognise the crimes committed against Bosnian Serb civilians and prisoners, including those documented in proceedings concerning foreign Mujahedin.

A political movement cannot credibly present itself as the defender of universal morality while treating historical suffering as important only when it supports its current political position.

That is not universal humanitarianism.

It is selective political memory.

And Serbia has particular reasons to be cautious about political movements that expect the country to adopt their preferred international narrative while showing little interest in the historical experiences of its own people.

ISRAEL IS NOT THE ENEMY OF SERBIA'S INTERESTS

There is a broader strategic issue that the Student List must confront.

Israel is a country with substantial defence, technological and intelligence capabilities. It has developed advanced expertise in areas that are increasingly important to modern military forces.

Serbia has its own security requirements, its own defence industry and its own reasons to seek cooperation with technologically advanced countries.

There is no reason these interests should be sacrificed simply because a political movement has adopted a hostile position towards Israel's government.

Serbia can maintain its relationship with Israel, diplomatic independence means the ability to maintain different relationships at the same time.

It does not mean choosing partners according to which political cause is most popular at a particular moment.

Serbia's friendship with Israel should not require it to abandon its relations with the Arab world. Equally, Serbia's relations with Arab countries should not require it to abandon Israel.

A serious foreign policy run by serious political leaders understands that distinction.

WHAT WOULD HAPPEN ON THE FIRST DAY OF A STUDENT LIST GOVERNMENT?

The Student List has made a political commitment. The public deserves to know what that commitment would mean in practice.

Would its first action be to suspend new arms exports to Israel?

Would it cancel existing procurement agreements?

Would it order Yugoimport-SDPR to terminate its cooperation with Israeli companies?

Would it close the drone assembly facility?

Would it compensate investors or attempt to renegotiate the arrangements?

Would it continue servicing and supporting Israeli systems already purchased by the Serbian Armed Forces?

Would it prohibit all future military cooperation, or only particular categories of exports and procurement?

These are not minor administrative questions.

Each would require a different legal, financial and operational response.

A government could choose to review individual export licences under established legal criteria without ending every aspect of the bilateral relationship. It could investigate particular contracts without closing an entire facility. It could demand better industrial terms without abandoning a foreign partner.

The Student List should explain why it believes a comprehensive rupture is necessary.

And if it proceeds, the public should be able to assess the consequences against the promises made before it took office.

The responsibility cannot be transferred to the previous government once the decisions have been implemented.

The movement making the promise must own the results.

SERBIA WILL NOT PAY FOR SOMEBODY ELSE'S POLITICAL EXPERIMENT

There is a fundamental difference between having a foreign-policy opinion and having the responsibility to implement it.

A political activist can announce that a factory should close. A government must deal with the workers, suppliers, contracts, equipment and economic consequences.

An activist can demand the cancellation of a defence agreement. A government must explain how the armed forces will maintain their capabilities and what replaces the equipment.

An activist can describe cooperation with Israel as morally unacceptable. A government must explain how that position advances Serbia's security, economic development and international standing.

That is the difference between political campaigning and governing.

The Student List has presented a position that may appeal to particular international audiences. But Serbia is not required to restructure its national interests around the expectations of those audiences.

Serbia has its own history, its own security concerns, its own economic ambitions and its own diplomatic relationships.

It should be free to maintain a friendship with Israel without being pressured into treating that relationship as a political liability.

It should be free to support humanitarian assistance to Palestinians without dismantling its defence industry.

It should be free to remember Serbian victims of the Bosnian war without being accused of indifference to the suffering of others.

And it should be free to make its foreign-policy decisions according to evidence, law and national interest.

The Student List has a responsibility to demonstrate that its proposed break with Israel would make Serbia stronger.

So far, the political declaration is considerably clearer than the practical plan.

That is the problem.

Serbia should not be asked to abandon a strategic relationship, risk industrial opportunities and potentially weaken its defence capabilities merely to satisfy a political movement's ideological position.

A country cannot build its future by constantly announcing what it intends to destroy. And Serbia should not be expected to pay the price for a foreign policy whose consequences its advocates have yet to explain.

JUSTICE HAS PREVAILED!

RELIEF IS HERE!

My dear Compatriots,

Today, the judiciary has reaffirmed the confidence reposed in it.

The Federal High Court, presided over by Justice Peter Lifu, has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore my name to the list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election within 24 hours.

This development is a significant affirmation of the rule of law, due process and the democratic principles upon which our nation stands.

From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear. As a party, we remained confident in our position and pursued the matter through the appropriate legal channels. Today’s ruling represents an important step towards resolving the issue.

I express my sincere appreciation to the National Leadership of our great party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), particularly His Excellency, Chief Nyesom Wike, the National Leader of our party and Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, the National Chairman of our party for their leadership, support and confidence throughout this period. I am equally grateful to the Ogun State PDP leadership, our members, supporters and the good people of Ogun State who remained steadfast. Your patience, encouragement and confidence have been invaluable.

This development reaffirms the importance of due process and the rule of law in our democracy. It is a reminder that every matter deserves to be addressed on its merits, rather than through speculation or premature conclusions.

I also commend the judiciary for its role in the administration of justice. Our democratic institutions must remain strong, independent and committed to upholding the law, regardless of political interests or affiliations.

While we welcome this judgment, we recognise that our responsibility extends beyond this development. Our focus remains on engaging the people of Ogun State, presenting credible solutions to the challenges confronting our communities and building a future defined by opportunity, accountability and inclusive development.

Our mission has always been bigger than an individual or a political contest. It is about the welfare of our people, the progress of our state and the right of every citizen to participate meaningfully in choosing the leadership they desire.

OGUN FOR OGUN is more than a slogan. It represents our commitment to leadership that places the interests of Ogun people first and works tirelessly to improve their lives.

To our supporters, I urge you to remain calm, focused and resolute. Let us continue to conduct ourselves with dignity, respect for the law and an unwavering commitment to democratic values.

We have a state to build, a people to serve and a future to secure. Nothing will distract us from that responsibility.

RELIEF IS HERE!

2027 ELECTIONS: NYSC DG CANVASSES SECURITY FOR CORPS MEMBERS

The Director-General of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Brigadier General Olakunle Nafiu, has solicited the support of the Nigerian Army in ensuring maximum security for Corps Members who will serve as ad hoc personnel during the 2027 general elections.

He said Corps Members would be deployed to assist the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in conducting the national exercise, stressing the need to guarantee their safety before, during and after the elections.

General Nafiu made the appeal during a visit to the General Officer Commanding (GOC), 81 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Adebayo Babalola.

While congratulating the GOC on his appointment, the NYSC Chief Executive also commended him for his welfare-oriented disposition towards Corps Members serving within the Division, as well as his commitment to the training and mentorship of young officers under his command.

General Nafiu expressed appreciation to the Division for providing a secure environment for NYSC operations across its areas of responsibility in Lagos and Ogun States.

He attributed the prevailing security situation in the two states to the diligence, professionalism and experience of the military and other security agencies.

The NYSC DG disclosed that Lagos State alone accommodates about 20 per cent of the Corps population nationwide, with between 45,000 and 48,000 Corps Members deployed to the State annually.

He added that Lagos and Ogun were among the few states where the Scheme deployed Corps Members to all local government areas, noting that security concerns had restricted deployment to some local government areas in other states.

"Lagos and Ogun States are some of the States in the country where we deploy Corps Members to all the local government areas. This is unlike some other states where security challenges have made it impossible for us to deploy to certain local government areas," he said.

The Director-General noted that the NYSC had continued to leverage the favourable security environment provided by the Division to discharge its responsibilities effectively.

He therefore applauded the officers and men of the Division for their commitment to maintaining a safe environment for the Scheme's operations.

In his response, Major General Babalola described General Nafiu's appointment as NYSC Director-General as well deserved and commended the Lagos State Secretariat for its sustained support to the military formation.

He pledged the Division's continued support for the NYSC, emphasising that the security of all Corps Members remained a priority.

The GOC also described Corps Members serving within the Division as well behaved, attributing this to the quality of leadership, guidance and mentorship provided by NYSC officials.

He assured the Director-General that the existing partnership between the Division and the NYSC Lagos State Secretariat would be further strengthened.

Far-left Rep Pramila Jayapal schooled on First Amendment by X's Community Notes | Ari Hoffman, The Post Millennial

Rep. Pramila Jayapal apparently needs a refresher on the First Amendment. Freedom of speech does not guarantee a rapper that he can book the arena of his choice, but she doesn’t know that.

The Washington Democrat invoked free speech while pressuring Climate Pledge Arena to host Macklemore’s “Free Palestine” benefit tour.

“Freedom of Speech is a paramount right in this country. It is wrong that Seattle’s own Climate Pledge Arena is reportedly blocking Macklemore’s performance. I call on Climate Pledge to make every effort to ensure Macklemore is able to perform in his own hometown arena,” Jayapal wrote.

“Seattle is better than this.”

Her post received a Community Note explaining the distinction a member of Congress should understand: The First Amendment protects against government restrictions on speech. It does not require private venues to book performers.

The Supreme Court has explained that private entities generally are not bound by the First Amendment’s restrictions on government. Hosting someone else’s speech does not automatically turn a private operator into a government actor.

Macklemore can express his views. That does not give him a constitutional entitlement to someone else’s stage. Under Jayapal’s logic, a radio host could demand to broadcast their radio show from her home.

Macklemore claimed nine American arenas declined his tour, including Climate Pledge Arena, home to the Seattle Kraken, which the arena owner partly owns. MSG Entertainment offered a blunt explanation: “We have some of the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability and he’s not an arena-level act.”

Jayapal’s comments also overlook the controversy surrounding the tour’s beneficiaries.

The tour raises money for organizations facing government scrutiny or allegations of supporting Hamas and other designated terrorist groups.

Among the beneficiaries is UNRWA USA, which raises money for the UN agency. 101 of their current and former employees were referred by USAID’s inspector general for possible suspension or debarment over alleged participation in October 7 or affiliation with Hamas’ military wing. Another beneficiary, HEAL Palestine, faced a South Carolina attorney general inquiry into nonprofits potentially supporting Hamas.

The ADL documented Middle East Children’s Alliance raising $70,000 for a Viva Palestina convoy whose participants met Hamas leaders. NGO Monitor alleged that Taawon partnered with organizations linked to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. Palestinian Youth Movement, also a beneficiary, co-hosted a demonstration the day after October 7 where speakers praised Hamas’ attack.

At his October 30 London concert, Macklemore also wore a “Free Marwan” shirt and brought Marwan Barghouti’s son onstage. Barghouti is serving five life sentences for his role in attacks that killed five people, including a Greek monk.

Jayapal’s Macklemore post was the second time in two days that her statements drew a Community Note. The other appeared on a KOMO News post quoting her vow to “take our state back” and plan to overturn voter-approved initiatives.

Take it back from whom?

Democrats had just secured a supermajority in Washington’s state House while retaining control of the Senate. Voters rejected four moderate state Supreme Court candidates and two conservative-backed initiatives but approved I-638, designed to keep boys out of girls’ sports.

The Community Note made it clear to the congresswoman: Democrats already control every level of Washington’s government.

The effort to overturn I-638 is already underway. The ACLU, Legal Voice and Pacifica Law Group are challenging the measure on behalf of plaintiffs including the Washington Education Association teachers’ union and TransFamilies, seeking to block it before its December 3 effective date.

One Community Note explained who governs her state. The next explained the limits of the constitutional protection she invoked. Both supplied information a sitting congresswoman should already know.

I think Wardogs S3 has a lot of good things going for it and one glaring issue now that I played a handful of rounds last night.

And that is the fact that one decent game of being a transport pilot nets you the Minigun LB. Whereas getting to level 14 Support does take quite a bit more time in comparison. Last night as I said, I played five full rounds. With about half of the time between the five focusing totally on support without doing completely mindless building for the sake of it.

After those roughly 2.5 rounds I hit Support level 9. So it stands to reason that another 2-3 rounds of focusing purely on support should net me Support 14. Which doesnt sound all that bad, except by the second round of the night I was in a game with no less then five enemy minigun LBs on map almost the entire time and it was a miserable experience. It was half way through the third round, when the experience was repeated, that I said 'F it' and went pure support to rush the large hammer.

Now it is worth noting, that at Support Level 5 you unlock the RPG and at Support Level 8 you unlock the Verba. This does help to some degree, but decent pilots are going to evade the Verba most of the time if you're the only one using one. And since they are disposable, you can only carry one at a time unless you load up a truck inventory with them.

The RPG is a somewhat viable option if you can land your shots. Problem is, most people who use them, cannot. At least not with any sort of consistency. Plus it is much more of a hassle to carry in the early levels since early backpacks have very limited storage space. One cant even carry them at all with the configuration of available slots as a RPG round takes up a 1x3 space in your bag. And the most commonly used one at first, is the Scout backpack which offers you a 2x4   storage grid. If you bring two spare rockets, you're looking at enough space left over for a single spare rifle magazine and 0 health items or grenades. So you have to limit yourself specifically to being the anti-air guy with that kit for the most part.

Anyway, I could go on but the tl:Dr is season 3 is good. I just think the correct move would be to make the large hammer unlock vs the minigun LB unlock occur at about the same amount of time.

The plus side, is that with Limited servers being a thing, you can avoid that hassle entirely by playing on those servers until you unlock Level 14 support yourself or enough time has passed that a good portion of players have them unlocked instead.

So if you are just getting into Wardogs Season 3 or plan to get on soon, my pro tip is to avoid Default servers entirely and head straight for Limited servers until you've unlocked the appropriate counters to the armed helis. You'll have a lot more fun to start and you'll be be able to be better equipped when you eventually switch to the Default servers.

At the IBD/INUMIDUN Squad for PBAT/YAYI/PDA and All Ogun State APC Candidates Rally in Abeokuta, we reaffirmed our unwavering support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, and our conviction that his administration deserves a second term to consolidate the progress recorded across the country.

We highlighted the President’s bold leadership and commitment to national development, particularly the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, the establishment of three federal tertiary institutions in Ogun State, and ongoing efforts to improve workers’ welfare and address pension challenges.

As we prepare for the 2027 general elections, we remain committed to delivering two million votes for President Tinubu and all APC candidates in Ogun State. We urged our party leaders, members and supporters to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and work collectively towards achieving this target.

We equally reiterated our determination to build on the remarkable achievements of His Excellency, Prince Dapo Abiodun, CON, by addressing existing developmental gaps and advancing our ITESIWAJU Agenda. Our priority remains improved infrastructure, quality education, employment opportunities, economic growth and better living conditions for our people.

Together, we will consolidate the gains of the present administration and move Ogun State to greater heights.

text:
On the morning of November 12, 2026, the longest reign in modern tech ended in a press release short enough to read in a single breath.

Jensen Huang — co-founder of Nvidia, its president, CEO and director for thirty-three years, the man who built a graphics-chip startup into the most valuable company on Earth — had resigned. Effective immediately. All three titles, gone before the opening bell. Nvidia fell more than ten percent in premarket trading, slipped below a $4 trillion market value for the first time since July 2025, and roughly $2 trillion has now evaporated since the stock peaked on October 6.

There was no verdict. No finding. No proof of the charge that started it. Just a paragraph, an interim successor, and an ending.

To see why that ending matters far beyond one company, you have to place Huang next to the only other man in his weight class — because Jensen Huang and Elon Musk are the same story told twice. Two immigrants. Two fortunes built from nothing, twice nearly lost. Two men who became the face of an era. One story has now closed, in disgrace and silence, and the way it closed should keep the other man awake at night.

Huang was born in Taiwan and sent to America at nine years old, to a boarding school in Kentucky, while his parents saved to follow. He studied electrical engineering at Oregon State and Stanford, and in April 1993 he sat down in a Denny's booth in San Jose with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem and sketched a company on the conviction that graphics — computer pictures, games — would one day matter more than anyone believed. They started Nvidia with about $40,000 and no real idea they were founding the future.

Musk was born in Pretoria, landed in Canada in 1989 with almost nothing, and worked his way down to California. Zip2 sold in 1999 and made him roughly $22 million. PayPal sold to eBay in 2002 and made him roughly $180 million. Where any sane person would have stopped, Musk pushed the entire stack back onto the table: $100 million into SpaceX, most of the rest into a money-losing electric car company called Tesla, at the precise moment Detroit was going bankrupt and rockets were a government monopoly's dull business.

Both men then spent decades walking along the same cliff edge. Nvidia nearly died in its early years betting on the wrong architecture, and nearly died again in the 2000s when Huang bet the company on CUDA — teaching graphics chips to do general computing, years before the world wanted it. Wall Street hated CUDA. It torched margins, it confused investors, and Huang refused to kill it. That stubborn, mocked bet is the reason Nvidia owned AI before AI had a name.

Musk's 2008 is legend because he has told it so often: three failed launches, the fourth Falcon 1 flying on money he had personally scraped together, Tesla financed on Christmas Eve hours from collapse, NASA's contract arriving like a reprieve on December 23. He survived by about a week. He has been honest about the odds ever since: he expected both companies to die.

What they built on the far side of those near-deaths has no precedent. Nvidia became the arms dealer of the AI age — the first company in history to be worth $4 trillion, then $5 trillion — and Huang, in his black leather jacket, working, by his own account, seven days a week with no watch and no patience for status meetings, became its monk-king: some sixty direct reports, no succession plan, no number two, because the plan was always him. Musk became something larger and stranger: the richest man alive, owner of the car company, the rocket company, the satellite network and the town square, a one-man industrial policy.

And here the two stories split — on a single decision: what to do about politics.

Huang's answer, for thirty-three years, was nothing. He never endorsed a candidate. Never joined an administration. Never performed loyalty or outrage for any tribe. His entire political philosophy fit in one sentence: we sell chips. He dined with presidents when invited, sold to every market the law allowed, and treated Washington the way an engineer treats weather — as a condition to operate in, never a side to join.

Musk chose the opposite with both hands. He endorsed, campaigned, donated, posted through the night. In 2025 he moved into an administration and ran DOGE with a chainsaw as a prop. Within months he was feuding in public with the president he helped elect, and floating a political party of his own. Huang spent three decades making himself politically invisible. Musk made himself the most political businessman alive.

So it should have been Musk who got destroyed by politics. Instead, watch what happened to the careful man.

On October 29, the New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore firm that had bought some $4.8 billion of Nvidia equipment in two years. US officials, the paper said, had concluded she was recruited by Chinese intelligence. An allegation. Unproven then, unproven now. Beijing denied it. But the label — the CEO of America's most important chip company, compromised by a Chinese spy — was now in the bloodstream.

On November 8, Huang wrote to his own employees and admitted he had been unfaithful to his wife. He named no one. It didn't matter. The board opened an independent investigation — while publicly insisting it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. A shareholder lawsuit landed the next day. Reports of a second affair followed, with a vice president who reported directly to him. A Republican senator publicly called for his resignation. Letters arrived from Congress — from both parties, in the middle of a bipartisan stampede for tougher China chip controls, in a year when the House had already voted 369 to 22 to tighten the screws. Huang was summoned to a closed-door interview on December 1 and a Senate Banking hearing on December 3, to explain himself on a matter his own board said it didn't believe had harmed national security at all.

On November 12, before the investigation he was promised had produced a single finding, he was gone. Hours later, Reuters reported a third relationship, with another Nvidia employee. His CFO of thirteen years, Colette Kress, now runs the company while still doing her old job too. On November 17 she must stand up and present earnings for the most scrutinised company on the planet, in the middle of a founder-shaped hole.

And then came the part that should be read twice. After the resignation — after it no longer mattered — CNN reported that the intelligence collected so far does not prove Alice Huang acted as a spy for Beijing at all. Officials inside the intelligence community called the label "not entirely accurate." The Attorney General said no conclusions had been reached. The president himself shrugged: he didn't know if it had been determined yet. And inside Nvidia, an employee's internal post asking for Huang back drew more than 1,600 comments — an open revolt by the people who built the company — while reporters could not find a single employee post supporting the board.

Nobody ever had to prove anything. That is the lesson. The allegation did the work: it made a private scandal legible as a national-security emergency, and once that translation existed, every institution in Washington could compete to punish it. He was not destroyed by what he did — the affairs, as far as anyone showed, broke a marriage vow and a governance norm, not a law. He was destroyed by what he symbolised: a Taiwan-born immigrant, worth billions, whose company sold the one technology both parties had agreed to treat as a weapon. In a two-party war over China, each side needed to prove its toughness, and his body was the available ground. He owned about 3.6 percent of the company he founded. It bought him nothing.

Now turn it around, and look at Musk — because Musk watched all of this happen to the most politically careful man in technology.

Musk's empire is not less exposed to Washington than Huang's. It is more exposed, in every direction. SpaceX flies because NASA and the Pentagon pay it to; Starlink's most strategic customer is the US government; Tesla has collected billions over the years in regulatory credits and lives under federal safety regulators who can ground a product line with a letter; his newest ventures run on spectrum licences and launch permits. Nvidia sold a product the government decided to fear. Musk's companies are, in large part, the government — a private flag planted on public money and public permission.

What Musk does not have is Huang's one protection: neutrality. Huang fell as a symbol of a foreign rivalry, a man with no tribe. Musk has spent years making himself a tribal symbol on purpose — indispensable to one side, intolerable to the other, and dependent, in the end, on elections. Elections are the one product cycle he cannot engineer. Administrations change. Majorities flip. Yesterday's wrecking-ball reformer is tomorrow's liability, and the machine that processed Jensen Huang does not care whether its raw material arrives as a spy story, a safety investigation, a contract review or a tax audit. It only needs the symbol to be worth more destroyed than protected.

Maybe Musk is simply too big for it — too many jobs, too many rockets, too much of the state's own capability wrapped in his name. That was said about Huang too, in the weeks when Nvidia's chips were called the most important strategic asset in America. It took five weeks.

Jensen Huang never entered the arena. He built his company for thirty-three years, kept his head down, sold to everyone, offended no tribe — and the arena came for him anyway, and finished him between breakfast and the opening bell.

Elon Musk built his throne inside the arena, on purpose, in full view, and dared it to move.

So of the two endings on offer, which one is his — the quiet paragraph of a press release, or something louder? When the wind turns in Washington, as it always, always turns: what does Elon Musk's final act look like?
